a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Affected Revision Frontier RF(E) as the set of knowledge objects potentially affected by a revision event, enabling incremental recomputation (Recalculate(RF(E))) instead of full-graph rebuilds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: change in NexusVersion affects migration/compatibility/patch compliance ... no reason to invalidate unrelated knowledge such as employee onboarding ... Revision propagation follows semantic dependencies
a_rows_sample.statement: Bounds revision propagation by semantic dependency (a version change affects migration/compatibility/patch-compliance knowledge but not unrelated domains like employee onboarding), mapped in DDD terms to explicit cross-bounded-context integration relationships rather than an uncontrolled global dependency graph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero=\varnothing ... Later, supporting evidence is invalidated ... Zero\neq\varnothing ... Zero is dynamic
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives a property of Zero under revision: a previously-satisfied requirement (Zero=∅) can reopen (Zero≠∅) when supporting evidence is later invalidated — 'Zero is dynamic,' representing the current epistemic gap, not a permanent requirement characteristic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_1=Migrate ... evidence supporting a prerequisite is invalidated ... DecisionAffected(D_1)=True ... should not automatically reverse the decision unless the applicable governance policy explicitly permits
a_rows_sample.statement: A prior decision (e.g. Migrate) whose supporting evidence is later invalidated becomes DecisionAffected=True, but automatic reversal requires explicit governance permission — the system may instead require review/pause/revocation/reassessment/no-action, 'preserving the distinction between computation and authority.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: \{Valid,Superseded,Questioned,Invalidated,Executed,Reversed\} ... Historical existence\neq Current validity
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-value decision-status lifecycle {Valid, Superseded, Questioned, Invalidated, Executed, Reversed}; historical decisions remain historical even if later invalidated — 'Historical existence ≠ Current validity.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS compute K_{t+1} from K_t and new evidence? ... K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,\Omega,EC)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central question of the step and defines the fundamental transition function K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC) where K_t=current state, E_t=new epistemic input, Omega=domain ontology/rules, EC=applicable epistemic contract.

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x EpistemicInput x Ontology x EpistemicContract

b_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Assertions,Evidence,Provenance,Relations,Assessments,Validity,TemporalState,Conflicts,Versions,Contracts,Policies)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects K={facts} in favor of an 11-component tuple K=(Assertions, Evidence, Provenance, Relations, Assessments, Validity, TemporalState, Conflicts, Versions, Contracts, Policies), with Decisions/Actions/Observations optionally included depending on whether event history is treated as part of state or an external log.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeState=DerivedState ... EventLog=HistoricalCause ... an important DDD distinction
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends keeping the event log conceptually separate from the derived KnowledgeState: Events_t and K_t=Fold(Events_0..t), giving KnowledgeState=DerivedState vs EventLog=HistoricalCause — 'an important DDD distinction.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10:00 Nexus=3.69, 11:00 Nexus=3.70, 12:00 Nexus=3.70 ... CurrentKnowledge\neq HistoricalKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a three-event history where the current state (3.70) differs from the full history (3.69->3.70), showing both are valuable — CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DeterministicUpdate ... our first major invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: States the first invariant: for fixed (K_t,E_t,Omega,EC), Update must produce the same K_{t+1} on repeated execution — DeterministicUpdate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RawInput\rightarrow LLM\rightarrow CandidateEvidence ... NonDeterministicAcquisition\rightarrow GovernedInput\rightarrow DeterministicStateTransition
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the LLM-nondeterminism concern: an LLM may participate before admission (RawInput->LLM->CandidateEvidence), but once admitted as a structured event E_t the transition is deterministic — 'one of the most important architectural boundaries we have discovered.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Update(Update(K,E),E)\equiv Update(K,E) ... idempotence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the second invariant, idempotence: applying the same evidence twice should not create artificial additional knowledge, Update(Update(K,E),E) ≡ Update(K,E), worked with a duplicate-database-record example resolved via EvidenceID(E1)=EvidenceID(E2) duplicate detection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Update must never destroy the source lineage ... Provenance(K)\supseteq Provenance(E)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the third invariant, provenance preservation: after E->A->K, Provenance(K) ⊇ Provenance(E) — 'Update must be provenance-preserving.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnresolvedConflict\rightarrow UnresolvedConflict unless new evidence or governance explicitly resolves it
b_rows_sample.statement: States the fourth invariant, contradiction preservation: contradictory same-time/context evidence with no resolution rule must remain an unresolved conflict rather than being silently resolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NoImplicitConflictResolution ... must not create A or B as the uniquely accepted truth merely because one looks more likely
b_rows_sample.statement: States the fifth invariant, no hallucinated resolution: given A⊥B with no authorized resolution rule, Update must not pick a winner because it 'looks more likely' — NoImplicitConflictResolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1} ... not always true ... naive monotonicity fails
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests naive monotonicity (K_t⊆K_{t+1}) against a version-change example (3.69->3.70 changes current state) and finds it fails.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_t\subseteq H_{t+1} ... History is monotonic; CurrentState need not be
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the sixth invariant into event-sourced monotonicity: historical event knowledge H_t is monotonic (events accumulate, history is never erased) even though current derived state is not — 'History is monotonic; CurrentState need not be' — 'a much better formulation.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_{t+1}=H_t\cup\{E_t\} ... K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},\Omega,EC) ... elegant
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the two-layer transition: H_{t+1}=H_t ∪ {E_t} (monotonic history growth) then K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},Omega,EC) (current state recomputation) — 'elegant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retract(E_1) ... Status(E_1)=Retracted ... K_{current} is recalculated
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines retraction: a source's later 'the previous record was incorrect' becomes Retract(E1), setting Status(E1)=Retracted (not deleting E1 from history), then recalculating K_current.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_2:Correction(E_1,3.69) ... preserve E_1 and record E_2 ... Correction\neq Deletion
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines correction as distinct from retraction/deletion: E2=Correction(E1,3.69) preserves E1 while recording the correcting event E2; the derived state may change to 3.69 — 'Correction ≠ Deletion.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: The certificate used to establish the evidence has been revoked ... EvidenceValidity(E)=False ... Assertion separate from EvidenceAssessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines revocation: a source can become invalid (e.g. a revoked certificate) without the proposition itself being false, EvidenceValidity(E)=False while the assertion remains historically recorded — demonstrates Assertion must be kept separate from EvidenceAssessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ValidFrom\le t<ValidUntil ... Expired\neq False
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines explicit validity intervals; when t>=ValidUntil the knowledge becomes Expired, explicitly distinct from False — 'this distinction is extremely important.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: True/Supported, False/Refuted, Unknown, Expired, Conflicted ... must not be collapsed into a single Boolean
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists (at least) five epistemic states that must not be collapsed into a single Boolean: Supported, Refuted, Unknown, Expired, and potentially Conflicted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal E=\{Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted\} ... I would not yet call this a simple lattice ... Expired does not necessarily mean Refuted
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a six-state epistemic space E={Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted} but explicitly declines to call it a simple lattice since some states are orthogonal dimensions (Expired does not imply Refuted; Retracted may concern evidence rather than assertion).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicState=(SupportStatus,ValidityStatus,ConflictStatus,TemporalStatus) ... much more expressive
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the epistemic-state space into a four-dimension tuple EpistemicState=(SupportStatus,ValidityStatus,ConflictStatus,TemporalStatus), worked with two example instantiations (one with ConflictStatus=none, one with ConflictStatus=conflicted) — 'much more expressive.'

a_aliases: Epistemic Error, Refutation, Retraction, Correction and Revision

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'epistemic-revision-error-taxonomy-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledge-state-closure-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: S0905's Step 25M: the six-way RevisionType taxonomy and revision-as-event-addition model, extending S0903's closure/state-machine invariants and S0904's distributed-retraction discussion into a full non-monotonic-knowledge treatment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The central question is: > When do two pieces of evidence constitute the same evidential contribution, when are they dependent transformations, and when are they genuinely independent observations?
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the file's governing problem: distinguishing same-contribution, dependent-transformation, and genuinely-independent evidence, calling it more fundamental than choosing an aggregation formula because getting it wrong makes 'every downstream confidence, conflict, gap, and conclusion' wrong.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity ... e_1=e_2 ... This is a data/infrastructure property. ... Equivalence ... e_1\sim e_2 ... Independence ... e_1\perp e_2 ... Equivalence\neq\text{Independence}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines three formally distinct evidence relations: Identity (e1=e2, literally the same record — same hash/document/observation ID, a data/infrastructure property), Equivalence (e1~e2, different records expressing the same underlying proposition, illustrated with two differently-worded documents both asserting Nexus 3.69), and Independence (e1⊥e2, genuinely separate information, illustrated by an API report and an independent filesystem inspection both reporting 3.69); concludes Equivalence ≠ Independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency is actually richer than equivalence ... Database → LLM → Architecture report → Human summary ... e_1\rightarrow e_2\rightarrow e_3\rightarrow e_4 ... Dependency\neq\text{Equivalence}
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a Database→LLM→Architecture-report→Human-summary chain that later items can causally/epistemically depend on earlier ones (e1→e2→e3→e4) while having different semantic content (e.g. 'Nexus=3.69' vs 'Nexus is running an older version'), so Dependency ≠ Equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need an Evidence Graph ... G_E=(V,E) ... V=\text{Evidence Objects} ... This graph is not merely metadata. It affects the mathematics of evidence aggregation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces an Evidence Graph G_E=(V,E) whose vertices are Evidence Objects and whose edges represent provenance/dependency (e.g. Nexus API observation --DERIVED_FROM--> LLM output --INTERPRETED_AS--> Assertion --REVIEWED_BY--> Human review), asserting the graph is not mere metadata but affects the mathematics of evidence aggregation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define the underlying observation ... UnderlyingObservation(e)=o ... means that these are multiple representations of one underlying observation. This is much more precise than simply saying "duplicate."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a function UnderlyingObservation(e)=o mapping an evidence record (database entry, screenshot, LLM extraction, human report) to the single underlying observation event it represents, offered as a more precise substitute for calling records 'duplicates'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence provenance becomes causal structure ... e_j\prec e_i ... Dependency\Rightarrow NonIndependent ... NonIndependent \not\Rightarrow DirectDependency ... Two sources can share a common ancestor without one directly producing the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines e_j≺e_i ('e_i was produced using e_j') and states the conservative rule Dependency⇒NonIndependent, while noting the converse fails: NonIndependent does not imply DirectDependency, because two sources can share a common ancestor without one producing the other directly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Common-source dependency ... Original document / LLM A, LLM B ... LLM_A\not\rightarrow LLM_B ... CommonAncestor(LLM_A,LLM_B) ... CommonSource(e_i,e_j) as a first-class relationship. This protects us against **correlated evidence inflation**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces CommonSource(e_i,e_j) as a first-class relationship for cases where two evidence items (e.g. LLM A and LLM B outputs) neither directly depend on each other but share a common ancestor document, warning that treating such items as independent corroboration causes correlated evidence inflation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three epistemic dependency classes ... Class 1 — Same contribution ... e_i\equiv e_j ... Count once. ... Class 2 — Dependent contribution ... e_i\leadsto e_j ... Do not treat them as independent corroboration. ... Class 3 — Independent contribution ... e_i\perp e_j ... They may contribute independen
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-class taxonomy for evidence-pair handling: Class 1 Same contribution (e_i≡e_j, count once), Class 2 Dependent contribution (e_i⤳e_j, never treat as independent corroboration), Class 3 Independent contribution (e_i⊥e_j, may contribute independently, explicitly qualified as 'under the selected policy').

a_rows_sample.anchor: UnknownDependency\neq\nIndependence ... UnknownDependency\Rightarrow Do\ not\ assume\ independent\ corroboration. This is a very strong candidate for a kernel invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the rule UnknownDependency ≠ Independence and, conservatively, UnknownDependency ⇒ do not assume independent corroboration, explicitly flagging this as 'a very strong candidate for a kernel invariant' for KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not say: > "Unknown dependency means the evidence is useless." That would be too strong. ... UnknownIndependence\neq NoEvidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an over-strong reading of the unknown-dependency rule: unknown dependency does not mean the evidence is useless — it means its incremental independent evidential contribution cannot be safely quantified, while the evidence may still be relevant, historically useful, supportive, contradictory, or useful for discovery; formalized as UnknownIndependence ≠ NoEvidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence Identity relation ... e_i\sim_E e_j ... Reflexivity ... Symmetry ... Transitivity ... \sim_E\text{ should be an equivalence relation} ... according to an explicitly declared equivalence policy ... because semantic equivalence is not always decidable automatically.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Evidence Identity relation e_i~_E e_j meant to satisfy reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity (a genuine equivalence relation), but qualifies this against an 'explicitly declared equivalence policy' since semantic equivalence is not always automatically decidable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is where LLMs become useful—but dangerous ... LLM: CandidateEquivalence(e1,e2) ... KnowledgeOS: EquivalenceStatus = Proposed ... Rule / human / deterministic check: Confirmed ... LLM\ judgment \neq authoritative epistemic fact
a_rows_sample.statement: Constrains the role of LLMs in establishing evidence equivalence: an LLM may propose CandidateEquivalence(e1,e2), which KnowledgeOS records as EquivalenceStatus=Proposed, but only a rule, human, or deterministic check can confirm it — 'LLM judgment ≠ authoritative epistemic fact'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD model ... Evidence ... Provenance ... EvidenceIdentity ... DependencyAssessment ... EvidenceAssessment ... Notice that **EvidenceAssessment does not contain Truth**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a DDD model with five entities — Evidence (EvidenceId, Proposition, Polarity, Source, AcquiredAt, Context, Quality), Provenance (parent/relation/transformation/actor/timestamp), EvidenceIdentity (UnderlyingObservationId, EquivalenceClass, IdentityConfidence), DependencyAssessment (EvidenceA/B, Relationship, Status, Basis), and EvidenceAssessment (PositiveSupport, NegativeSupport, Uncertainty, DependencyStructure, Quality, Qualifications) — and explicitly notes EvidenceAssessment does not contain Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematical structure emerging ... \mathcal E \rightarrow \mathcal E/\sim_E \rightarrow D \rightarrow Q \rightarrow \oplus_\rho \rightarrow EA ... This is becoming a genuine computational calculus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assembles the pipeline: raw evidence set E, quotient by equivalence E/~_E, dependency function D:(E/~_E)^2→{Dependent,Independent,Unknown}, quality function Q:E/~_E→Q, policy-specific aggregation ⊕_ρ, producing an EvidenceAssessment EA — described as 'becoming a genuine computational calculus'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One thing we must NOT do ... Independent(e_i,e_j) = SemanticDifference(e_i,e_j) ... Sensor A: temperature = 20°C Sensor B: temperature = 20°C ... Same proposition. Different observations. ... SemanticEquivalence\neq EvidentialIndependence. This distinction is fundamental.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against the mathematically wrong definition Independent(e_i,e_j)=SemanticDifference(e_i,e_j), using two sensors reporting the identical 20°C reading as independent observations of the same proposition to establish SemanticEquivalence ≠ EvidentialIndependence as a fundamental distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Our new test cases ... Case A — Exact duplicate ... Case B — Semantic duplicate ... Case C — Independent identical observations ... Case D — LLM transformation ... Case E — Common-source outputs ... Case F — Unknown provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Lays out six test cases with expected contribution counts: (A) exact duplicate e1=e2 → 1 contribution; (B) semantic duplicate e1~_E e2 → 1 contribution; (C) independent identical observations e1~_P e2 but e1⊥e2 → 2 contributions; (D) LLM transformation e1→LLM(e1) → 1 independent contribution; (E) common-source outputs e0→e1, e0→e2 → not independent; (F) unknown provenance → do not assume independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A provisional theorem ... Evidence multiplicity is not equivalent to evidential independence. ... |E| \neq |\text{IndependentContributions}(E)| ... InformationVolume\neq EvidenceStrength ... Ten documents copied from one source do not necessarily provide ten pieces of evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a provisional theorem that evidence multiplicity is not equivalent to evidential independence, formalized as |E| ≠ |IndependentContributions(E)| and InformationVolume ≠ EvidenceStrength, illustrated by ten documents copied from one source not necessarily providing ten pieces of evidence; called 'a very important KnowledgeOS principle'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where we are now ... Strongly established: Evidence Identity, Evidence Equivalence, Evidence Dependency, Common-Source Detection, Unknown Dependency ... Still open ... How can KnowledgeOS computationally determine independence? ... Absolute epistemic independence is generally not computable from arb
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes five 'strongly established' concepts (Evidence Identity, Equivalence, Dependency, Common-Source Detection, Unknown Dependency) and states the remaining open question — how KnowledgeOS can computationally determine independence — with the explicit limitation that absolute epistemic independence is generally not computable from arbitrary documents alone, framed as 'a boundary condition of the problem' rather than a KnowledgeOS failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the next step should be to define an **Operational Independence Test**: Independence_\rho(e_i,e_j,G_E,C) \rightarrow \{Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown\} ... test whether that operation is actually implementable from our available inputs: documents, databases, Internet sources, rules, manifests, human ins
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the next step: define an Operational Independence Test Independence_ρ(e_i,e_j,G_E,C)→{Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown} and test its implementability against KnowledgeOS's actual available inputs (documents, databases, Internet sources, rules, manifests, human instructions, scope, constitution, settings, ADRs, textbooks, AI/LLM outputs) as 'the next computational-closure test' — directly taken up by the immediately following file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 2 ... How does KnowledgeOS determine whether two evidence items are the same underlying evidential contribution, merely semantically equivalent, or genuinely distinct observations? That takes us into the Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... I suggest we tackle that next—and test it with
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes by posing Step 2's question — same underlying evidential contribution vs semantic equivalence vs genuinely distinct observation — as the Evidence Identity/Equivalence Calculus, to be tackled next via concrete examples rather than abstract definition; taken up by the immediately following file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS determine whether two evidence items are independent using computable information? ... True Independence ... Operationally Established Independence ... KnowledgeOS cannot generally prove metaphysical independence. It can determine independence relative to an explicit evidence model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes True (metaphysical) Independence, which KnowledgeOS cannot generally prove, from Operationally Established Independence, which it can determine relative to an explicit evidence model; defines Ind_ρ(e_i,e_j,G,C)→{Independent,Dependent,Unknown} over evidence pair, provenance graph G, context C, and independence policy ρ.

type_signature.domain: Evidence x Evidence x Graph x Context

b_rows_sample.anchor: What information can KnowledgeOS actually inspect? ... M(e)=(Source,AcquisitionEvent,Timestamp,Actor,Method,ParentEvidence,Transformation,Location,Content,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the inspectable evidence-metadata tuple M(e)=(Source, AcquisitionEvent, Timestamp, Actor, Method, ParentEvidence, Transformation, Location, Content, Context), illustrated by contrasting a direct Nexus-API observation with an LLM summarization whose Parent is that observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The first deterministic rule ... If e_i\leadsto e_j in the provenance graph, then Ind(e_i,e_j)=Dependent. This is deterministic. No LLM is required.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a deterministic rule requiring no LLM: if e_i leads to e_j in the provenance graph (e.g. Database → LLM extraction), then Ind(e_i,e_j)=Dependent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Common ancestry ... CommonAncestor(A,B)=D ... we cannot safely say A\perp B ... CommonAncestor(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow Independent(e_i,e_j)\neq Confirmed ... The result should normally be Unknown unless the policy provides a justified way to establish conditional independence.
b_rows_sample.statement: For two evidence items with no direct edge but a common ancestor (e.g. two LLMs, A and B, both reading Document D), states CommonAncestor(e_i,e_j) ⇒ Independent(e_i,e_j)≠Confirmed, with the default result Unknown unless the policy justifies conditional independence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different sources do not automatically mean independent ... Reuters → Document A, Reuters → Document B ... Source(A)\neq Source(B) does not prove A\perp B ... DifferentSource\not\Rightarrow Independent
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that different apparent sources (e.g. two documents both ultimately from Reuters) do not prove independence, since both may originate from the same underlying report: DifferentSource ⇏ Independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different acquisition events are stronger ... Sensor A → 20°C at 10:00, Sensor B → 20°C at 10:00 ... independent sensors; independent acquisition mechanisms; independent provenance; no shared upstream observation. Then we can establish OperationallyIndependent(e_1,e_2) under the declared policy. Not
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows that independent acquisition mechanisms/provenance (e.g. two separate sensors reporting the same 20°C reading with no shared upstream observation) can establish OperationallyIndependent(e1,e2) under a declared policy, stressing the qualifier 'operationally'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need an independence evidence vector ... I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) ... Source independence ... Acquisition independence ... Provenance independence ... Method independence ... Temporal independence ... Common-ancestor status ... Each can be {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}. This
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing independence not as a single boolean but as a six-dimension vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) — Source, Acquisition, Provenance, Method, Temporal independence and Common-ancestor status — each valued {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}, to preserve uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Why not simply calculate an independence score? We should resist IndependenceScore=0.87 because that number would obscure why the evidence is considered independent. ... This is much more auditable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues against collapsing independence into a single score like IndependenceScore=0.87, since a scalar obscures why evidence is considered independent, in favor of an itemized per-dimension Confirmed/Rejected breakdown that is auditable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formal decision rule ... Ind_\rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) = Dependent if dependency is established; Independent if all required independence conditions hold; Unknown otherwise. The important word is required ... because the conditions depend on policy. For a high-risk security decision, we may require very str
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the formal decision rule for Ind_ρ as a three-way case split (Dependent/Independent/Unknown) keyed on policy-defined 'required' conditions, noting the required strength of independence is itself policy-dependent (e.g. stronger for high-risk security decisions than exploratory research).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three-valued result is important ... I=\{I,D,U\} ... better than {True,False} because Unknown\neq False and Unknown\neq True. ... Absence of evidence for independence is not evidence of dependence, but neither is it evidence of independence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the three-valued result set {Independent, Dependent, Unknown} is necessary rather than a boolean, since Unknown≠False and Unknown≠True, stating the central KnowledgeOS principle: 'Absence of evidence for independence is not evidence of dependence, but neither is it evidence of independence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD representation ... IndependenceAssessment ... EvidenceA, EvidenceB, SourceRelation, AcquisitionRelation, ProvenanceRelation, MethodRelation, CommonAncestor, Result, Policy, Basis, Timestamp ... The result is a domain object, not merely a database flag.
b_rows_sample.statement: Models the independence determination as an IndependenceAssessment domain object (EvidenceA/B, per-dimension relation fields, CommonAncestor, Result, Policy, Basis, Timestamp) rather than a bare database flag.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain invariant ... Dependent(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow \neg Independent(e_i,e_j) ... Unknown(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow \neg ConfirmedIndependent(e_i,e_j). The second is particularly important.
b_rows_sample.statement: States two formal invariants: Dependent(e_i,e_j) ⇒ ¬Independent(e_i,e_j), and Unknown(e_i,e_j) ⇒ ¬ConfirmedIndependent(e_i,e_j), flagging the second as particularly important.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test cases ... Case A — Exact duplicate ... Dependent/SameContribution ... Case B — LLM transformation ... Dependent ... Case C — Two LLMs reading the same document ... Unknown ... Case D — Two independent sensors ... Independent ... Case E — Two websites copying the same source ... Dependent/Correl
b_rows_sample.statement: Works six test cases through Ind_ρ: (A) exact duplicate → Dependent/SameContribution; (B) e2=LLM(e1) → Dependent; (C) two LLMs reading the same document D → Unknown (absent a conditional-independence policy); (D) two independent sensors → Independent under policy; (E) two websites copying one source → Dependent/Correlated; (F) missing provenance → Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us an important KnowledgeOS law ... Independence must be established, not assumed. ... Independence(e_i,e_j)=Confirmed only when the declared policy's conditions are satisfied. Otherwise Unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally adopts the KnowledgeOS law 'Independence must be established, not assumed', formalized as Independence(e_i,e_j)=Confirmed only when the declared policy's conditions are satisfied, else Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One subtle statistical correction ... Operational independence is not necessarily statistical independence. ... both may be affected by the same environmental bias. OperationallyIndependent \not\Rightarrow StatisticallyIndependent ... OperationalIndependence \rightarrow Evidence about possible stati
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a key caveat: OperationallyIndependent does not imply StatisticallyIndependent (e.g. two sensors with separate acquisition/hardware may still share an environmental bias); operational independence only provides evidence about possible statistical independence, and a Bayesian factorization P(E1,E2|H)=P(E1|H)P(E2|H) needs its own justified assumptions — hence Evidence Architecture and Statistical Inference Policy must be kept separate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 1 conclusion ... operational independence is computable in a qualified sense. ... it must not claim universal statistical independence merely from metadata.
b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes Step 1: KnowledgeOS can deterministically inspect provenance, dependency, common ancestry, acquisition events, sources, methods, and context to produce Independent/Dependent/Unknown under a declared policy, but must never claim universal statistical independence from metadata alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 2 ... How does KnowledgeOS determine whether two evidence items are the same underlying evidential contribution, merely semantically equivalent, or genuinely distinct observations? That takes us into the Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... I suggest we tackle that next—and test it with
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes by posing Step 2's question — same underlying evidential contribution vs semantic equivalence vs genuinely distinct observation — as the Evidence Identity/Equivalence Calculus, to be tackled next via concrete examples rather than abstract definition; taken up by the immediately following file.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'operational-independence-test' POSSIBLY relates to 'evidence-identity-equivalence-dependency-calculus' (batch B0021). Note: S0855's Step 1: operationalizes independence as a three-valued, policy-relative, six-dimension-vector function over evidence metadata and provenance graphs; explicitly distinguishes operational from statistical independence; sets up Step 2 (evidence identity/equivalence calculus).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I treated MD-058 and MD-059 as the frozen handover boundary and used only their recorded evidence/provenance and the primary corpus sources they explicitly relied upon. I did not perform new theory, reconciliation, model selection, F3<->F4 bridging, external literature research, or implementation. F4 is semantically instantiated in form, but not closed enough to make its satisfaction semantics computable; and it is not yet typed into a common observation space with F3. The two remaining blockers are therefore distinct: internal F4 closure and cross-model bridging.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the audit's decisive finding and self-imposed scope boundary: F4 is instantiated in form but not computationally closed, and separately not yet typed into a common observation space with F3 -- two genuinely distinct blockers (internal F4 closure vs cross-model bridging), both named by MD-059 as separate unauthorized next acts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F4 completeness matrix A-K: A K_t variant census PARTIALLY FOUND (9+ mutually unreconciled variants, only 1 of 11 named components concretely typed); B component semantics NOT FOUND (only Sigma_t=(A,S,R,V,C) concretely defined, in one variant only); C relationships among variants CONFLICTING (mutually unreconciled, no component-level consistency established); D corpus-grounded common semantic core NOT FOUND; E R_t semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (Req(EC_t) exists as formal input but satisfaction predicates remain multiply defined/contested); F Sat(K_t,r) semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (shape frozen, but computing Sat requires K_t component semantics which are incomplete -- defined in form but not computationally closed); G decomposition-independent Sat NOT FOUND (the principal internal F4 blocker); H K_t->K_{t+1} transition semantics CONFLICTING (delta(K_t,e_t) and the P-12/P-13 family unresolved); I F4 Obs PARTIALLY FOUND (constructible in form, not computable); J F4 Beh PARTIALLY FOUND (general slot exists, no executable F4 Beh, classified UNAVAILABLE); K F4 Trace PARTIALLY FOUND (general machinery exists, no F4-specific instances).
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full eleven-item (A-K) F4 completeness matrix distinguishing what exists in form/shape from what is computationally closed across the K_t variant census, component semantics, R_t/Sat semantics, and F4's Obs/Beh/Trace, concluding this is why MD-059 did not describe F4 as simply absent -- the semantic shell is real but instantiation is incomplete.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F3<->F4 readiness matrix L-Q: L F3 observation semantics FOUND (Beh_c(K):=Reach(Ops(K)), the only candidate with real instantiated semantics); M F4 observation semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (formally constructible, not computable since Sat is not closed); N atoms<->requirements bridge NOT FOUND (F3 outputs reached atoms, F4 outputs satisfied requirements, no corpus document bridges these types); O common observation domain NOT FOUND (different codomains, no common Q,O can be posed without inventing the bridge); P common behaviour/trace domain NOT FOUND (F3 has instantiated behaviour, F4 does not); Q formal F3<->F4 equivalence relation NOT FOUND (MD-058 derived the general shape Obs-equality but not the corpus-intended ≡, and its cross-candidate matrix left all 15 pairs unresolved).
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full six-item (L-Q) F3<->F4 readiness matrix, establishing F3 as the only model with real instantiated observation semantics and F4 as merely formally constructible, with the critical N/O finding that F3 and F4 currently have no corpus-grounded bridge between their output types (atoms vs satisfied requirements) at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 approx_{Q,O} K2 iff Obs_{Q,O}(K1)=Obs_{Q,O}(K2). But this is not a completed F3<->F4 equivalence result. MD-058 explicitly says that Q,O remain open and that this does not recover the corpus-intended stronger equiv. So: The equivalence machinery exists; the F3/F4 semantic inputs required to instantiate it do not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that MD-058's general equivalence formula (K1 approx K2 iff their Q,O-relative observations match) is real mathematics but not itself a completed F3<->F4 equivalence result, since the Q,O parameters remain open and cannot recover the corpus-intended stronger equivalence relation -- the machinery exists but the semantic inputs to instantiate it do not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GA-001/GA-038 readiness R-T: R evidence sufficient for GA-001 NOT FOUND (MD-059 sharpened this to a type mismatch: atoms vs requirements); S evidence sufficient for GA-038 NOT FOUND (MD-023 found no corpus-justified canonicalization criterion, the sole positive precedent being explicit governance ratification of Delta_t, not mathematical selection); T evidence to compare F4 with another candidate beyond F3 NOT FOUND (all 15 pairwise comparisons in MD-058's matrix remained unresolved). GA-001 is blocked by missing comparable semantic types, not by lack of an equivalence formula. GA-038 is also not a hidden computational problem at present ... GA-038 cannot legitimately be marked solved merely because F4 becomes computable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assesses both higher-level governance objectives GA-001 and GA-038 as unchanged/blocked, sharply distinguishing GA-001's blocker (a named type mismatch between atoms and requirements, not a missing equivalence formula) from GA-038's blocker (absence of any corpus-grounded canonicalization criterion, with the only successful precedent being governance ratification rather than mathematical selection), and explicitly warning that F4 becoming computable would not by itself solve GA-038.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The externally supplied analysis encountered during MD-059 must not be counted as independent corroboration. MD-059 established that it: was created the same day, explicitly cited MD-058, was therefore a response to MD-058 rather than prior evidence, was classified as same-day, MD-058-consuming re-analysis. It is useful as a cross-check, but not admissible as independent corroboration of the F4 state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a strict provenance rule: an externally supplied analysis encountered during MD-059, though created the same day and citing MD-058, is classified as same-day/MD-058-consuming re-analysis rather than independent prior evidence, and is therefore admissible only as a cross-check, never as independent corroboration of F4's state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-15] is in M0043, a primary corpus source dated 2026-09-02. MD-059 discovered it on 2026-09-09. Therefore: the discovery was same-day relative to MD-059; the underlying evidence predates MD-059; it is not derivative of MD-059. It corrected MD-058's provenance interpretation, but did not invalidate MD-058's mathematical derivation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws a fine provenance distinction for [DEF-15]: although discovered the same day as MD-059, its underlying evidence (M0043, dated 2026-09-02) genuinely predates MD-059, so it counts as legitimate prior evidence (unlike the externally-supplied same-day analysis) that corrects MD-058's provenance interpretation without invalidating its mathematical derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: theory-extraction/ / Lane-T K3 / Omega / T-K1 / T-K2 -- MD-059 explicitly kept these firewalled throughout. Therefore those materials must not silently become F4 evidence in this handover.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes that materials from another research lane (Lane-T / theory-extraction, including K3/Omega/T-K1/T-K2) were explicitly firewalled by MD-059 and must not be silently absorbed as F4 evidence in this or any handover.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)} -- Defined and frozen. This is not the blocker. Sat(K_t,r) -- Defined in shape, not computationally closed. defined != computable. Obs_F4 -- Constructible in form, not computable. That is stronger than 'not found' but weaker than 'implemented.' Beh_F4/Trace_F4 -- General semantic slots exist; F4-specific instantiation unavailable. F3<->F4 -- Not merely untested. It is presently ill-typed as a comparison because Obs_F3 subseteq reached atoms while Obs_F4 subseteq satisfied requirements. There is no corpus-grounded mapping between these spaces.
a_rows_sample.statement: States five precise state distinctions to preserve exactly: Delta_t is frozen and not the blocker; Sat is defined-in-shape but not computable (defined != computable); Obs_F4 is constructible-but-not-computable (a third state between 'not found' and 'implemented'); Beh_F4/Trace_F4 have general slots but no F4-specific instantiation; and the F3<->F4 comparison is not merely untested but presently ill-typed, since Obs_F3 and Obs_F4 live in different, unbridged codomains (reached atoms vs satisfied requirements).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimal remaining dependency chain: K_t component semantics -> decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) -> computable F4 Obs_F4 -> [F4 Beh_F4/Trace_F4 <- transition/composition semantics] -> F4 semantic instantiation -> [F3 observation semantics, F4 observation semantics] -> atoms<->requirements -> common observation domain -> well-posed F3<->F4 comparison -> cross-model equivalence -> [GA-001, evidence relevant to GA-038 but NOT sufficient by itself]. F4 completion does not automatically solve GA-038. GA-001 cannot be reached merely by having Obs_F4; the atom/requirement type mismatch still has to be resolved by admissible evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lays out the full minimal dependency chain from K_t component semantics through to GA-001/GA-038, explicitly stating this reconstructs an existing corpus-supported chain rather than introducing a new one, and reiterating that neither GA-001 nor GA-038 follows automatically even once F4 is completed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MD-059 records: 1. reconcile the 9+ K_t variants enough to provide a decomposition-independent Sat body; 2. build the missing atoms<->requirements bridge. For the smallest fundamental blocker, the first act is prior: Research Act: establish whether the existing corpus contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) semantics across the existing K_t variants. Without Sat, Obs_F4 is not computable. Without Obs_F4, F4 has no comparable instantiated observation semantics. Without F4 semantics, the F3<->F4 comparison cannot advance. GA-001 therefore cannot advance through F4. The atoms<->requirements bridge is a second, independent blocker, but even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat(K_t,r) computable. That research act has not been executed here.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the single smallest fundamental next research act as determining whether the existing corpus already contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) (prior to actually reconciling the 9+ K_t variants), arguing it is logically prior to the separately-needed atoms<->requirements bridge since even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat computable; explicitly states this act has not been executed in this document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The historical corpus does contain more of the backbone than the earlier handover stated. The important correction is that the remaining problem is not absence of notation or conceptual primitives; it is the absence of a closed, mutually typed, F4-specific operational composition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the earlier handover's framing: the historical corpus contains substantially more semantic backbone (notation and conceptual primitives) than previously credited; the actual remaining problem is the absence of a closed, mutually typed, F4-specific operational composition linking those primitives, not their absence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t in K-blackboard, K-blackboard = space of admissible semantic epistemic states. It explicitly refuses to make K_t universally equal to a tuple and instead distinguishes semantic state from representation. K_t=(Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status) but explicitly a semantic decomposition, not a mandatory storage tuple. The most explicit later Model-B form is the 11-component tuple K_t=(A_t,R_t,E_t,Sigma_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t,T_t,G_t,C_t,M_t), but that family is not selected by the abstract DEF-11 formulation. Verdict: K_t in K-blackboard FOUND-UNTYPED; Concrete Model-B K_t CONFLICTING. There is no evidence selecting one concrete Model-B formulation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the historical corpus defines K_t as an abstract semantic epistemic state (K_t in K-blackboard, deliberately not reduced to a mandatory tuple, with a ten-field semantic decomposition explicitly marked non-mandatory) alongside a separate, unselected 11-component concrete Model-B tuple family, verdict FOUND-UNTYPED for the abstract form and CONFLICTING for the concrete family, with no evidence selecting between the concrete formulations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: r(K_t)=x_t. Representation carrier (X_r, A_r) and family R-script={R_r: r in R}, R_r: K-blackboard <-> X_r. No single representation is automatically the KnowledgeOS ontology. Missing: the mathematical type of r; whether every r is a function; whether R_r is total/partial/injective/surjective/invertible/merely relational; the precise type of x_t; admissibility conditions. Notation collision: in representation theory r denotes a representation; in gap theory r denotes an epistemic requirement r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity). The corpus does not establish that these two uses of r are the same object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the representation function r(K_t)=x_t with a representation carrier and family, explicitly noting no representation is automatically canonical, but leaves the mathematical type of r, its totality/injectivity/invertibility properties, and x_t's precise type unclosed; identifies a genuine notation collision where 'r' denotes a representation in one theory and a seven-field epistemic requirement in another, with the corpus never establishing these are the same object. Verdict: FOUND-UNTYPED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Obs: O_t^s = Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t), and epistemic observables as functions in a measurable setting. But this does not establish Obs_F4: K-blackboard -> O_F4. There is no historical rule showing that Obs_F4(K_t) is obtained from r(K_t)=x_t, from EC, or from Sat. Verdict: Generic Obs FOUND-TYPED; F4-specific Obs_F4 NOT FOUND.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds a generic, formally typed historical Obs function (O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t)) but no rule deriving an F4-specific Obs_F4 from any of r(K_t), EC, or Sat, verdict: generic Obs FOUND-TYPED, F4-specific Obs_F4 NOT FOUND.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC_t = EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t), the epistemic contract, used to define I(EC_t)={K in K-blackboard: Sat(K,EC_t)} and Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t). Missing: contract structure present; contract construction algorithm absent; fully grounded Sat only partial. No source establishes that EC_t is identical to C_KOS. They should therefore remain separate. Verdict: EC FOUND-UNTYPED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the epistemic contract EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) with its role in defining an admissible ideal region and adequacy, but finds no construction algorithm for EC_t and no evidence that EC_t is identical to C_KOS (the two should remain separate concepts), verdict FOUND-UNTYPED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ten Sat questions -- decisive audit: 1. Domain of K_t? K-blackboard proposed, exact structure OPEN. 2. Type of r? seven-field tuple proposed. 3. Codomain? {0,1} explicitly proposed; competing top/bot/U sub-semantics also exist. 4. Total/partial? NOT ESTABLISHED. 5. Evidence required? categories discussed, no complete evaluator. 6. Meaning of 1? requirement satisfied. 7. Meaning of 0? requirement unsatisfied. 8. Insufficient evidence? NOT CLOSED, candidate Unknown semantics exist. 9. Is UNKNOWN distinct? general theory yes, F4 Sat treatment NOT ESTABLISHED. 10. Deterministic/reproducible? NO -- no complete evaluation algorithm. Two engineers cannot currently compute the same Sat(K_t,r) from corpus-defined rules alone.
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a ten-question decisive audit of Sat(K_t,r) against the historical corpus, finding the codomain itself contested (binary {0,1} vs a ternary top/bot/Unknown sub-semantics with no authorized selection), totality/evidence-sufficiency/insufficient-evidence-treatment all unclosed, and concludes with a definitive negative reproducibility test: two engineers cannot currently compute the same Sat(K_t,r) result from corpus-defined rules alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t: Sat(K_t,r)=0}. It is the strongest historical F4 formula and was subsequently frozen as a constraint. R_t typed? PARTIALLY/candidate-typed. Sat typed? PARTIALLY; codomain conflicting. Sat executable? NO. Delta_t formula defined? YES. Delta_t executable? NO. Therefore: defined Delta_t != computable Delta_t. Verdict: Delta_t FOUND-UNTYPED as an operational object. The set-formula exists, but its evaluation cannot yet be executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Delta_t's set-builder formula is the strongest, frozen historical F4 formula, but derives via a five-row dependency table that it is not executable since Sat is not executable, establishing the sharp distinction defined Delta_t != computable Delta_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transition semantics: K_{t+1}=T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t) and H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}; also K_{t+1}=Transition(K_t,Operation,Parameters) with remaining work to define exact operation semantics/pre/postconditions; also H_t=(e_0,...,e_{t-1}), H_{t+1}=H_t || e_t, Replay(K_0,H_t)=K_t. These must not be collapsed: T, delta, Transition, event-based, operation-based, history, replay are not established as one formally identical transition system. The later persistence audit explicitly records that the tau_1..tau_11 items are transition CLASSES, not functions. Do not equate the tau classes with delta.
a_rows_sample.statement: Catalogs at least four distinct historical transition-semantics formulations (T-based, event-based Transition/Operation, history-append with Replay, and tau_1..tau_11 transition classes) and explicitly warns against collapsing them into one formally identical transition system, particularly against equating the tau classes (transition classes, not functions) with delta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Theory is the formal theory ... to answer: How can a system represent, transform, evaluate, preserve, revise, and act upon knowledge without confusing reality, information, evidence, truth, determination, decision, and action? It is not yet a finished universal 'Knowledge Algebra.' The strongest current form is a theory of epistemic state, representation, evidence, inquiry, propositions, and transformations, with some parts still explicitly research-stage.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central question KnowledgeOS Theory answers and its current honest scope: a theory of epistemic state/representation/evidence/inquiry/propositions/transformations, explicitly not yet a finished universal Knowledge Algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Information -> Representation -> Proposition -> Evidence -> Warrant/Reasoning -> KnowledgeState -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> NewEvidence. Evidence is not Truth. Observation is not Evidence. Representation is not Ontology. Determination is not Truth unless a soundness bridge has been established. Decision is not Determination. Decision is not Action. Unknown is not False. Correlation is not Causation. A graph is not automatically a Knowledge State. A path is not automatically an inference. Hash equality is not semantic identity. These distinctions prevent the system from making epistemic category errors.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the fourteen-stage conceptual chain from Reality to NewEvidence and eleven protective non-identities (Evidence!=Truth, Observation!=Evidence, Representation!=Ontology, Determination!=Truth without a soundness bridge, Decision!=Determination, Decision!=Action, Unknown!=False, Correlation!=Causation, graph!=KnowledgeState, path!=inference, hash-equality!=semantic-identity), framed as preventing epistemic category errors.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status), but this is currently treated as a semantic decomposition, not necessarily a mandatory implementation tuple. Knowledge State != Representation. Different representations may potentially represent the same semantic state. But the theory is deliberately cautious: semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations has not been universally established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the K_t semantic decomposition (explicitly non-mandatory) and the Knowledge State != Representation principle, cautioning that semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations is not universally established -- directly consistent with this same batch's F4 audit findings on equiv_sem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [[s]]_Gamma = p where s is a representation/sentence and p is the proposition interpreted under context Gamma. Truth(p,w,Gamma,t) in {0,1}. This allows the theory to distinguish assertion != determination != truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the proposition-interpretation formalization [[s]]_Gamma=p and truth evaluation Truth(p,w,Gamma,t), supporting the three-way distinction assertion != determination != truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) meaning that evidence e bears upon proposition p under context Gamma at time t. Evidence != Truth and Evidence != Knowledge. two pieces of evidence != two independent pieces of evidence. Two documents may simply copy the same original source. path != independent evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates evidence as a relational predicate Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) rather than a property of an object, deriving Evidence!=Truth, Evidence!=Knowledge, and the independence warning that multiple evidence items copying the same source do not constitute independent corroboration, nor does a mere graph path constitute independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q=<X,Y,Gamma,tau,Pi,Lambda> and more fundamentally an inquiry can be understood as an answer-producing function q:W->Y. This leads to the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy. A representation does not have to preserve everything. It has to preserve what is necessary to answer the inquiry correctly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the inquiry formalization as a six-tuple and as an answer-producing function q:W->Y, grounding the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy (a representation need only preserve what answers the inquiry correctly, not everything).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T:X->X' transforms a representation. Q=g o T where Q is the inquiry-relevant observable. The preservation condition can be expressed as Pi o T = Pi o T o E_S for an appropriate elimination/reduction structure. This provides the foundation for reasoning about reduction, elimination, equivalence, sufficient representations, preservation, semantic invariants, and Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the transformation and preservation formalization (T:X->X', Q=g∘T, the preservation condition Pi∘T=Pi∘T∘E_S), naming it the foundation for the whole reduction/elimination/equivalence/Zero research family already covered extensively in this batch's kr-rep-reduction-related documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not simply the number 0. A Knowledge Gap can be represented as a set of unsatisfied requirements: Delta_t = {r in R_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. Then Delta_t=empty means that there is no remaining requirement gap under the relevant satisfaction semantics. Zero equiv empty gap rather than merely numerical zero. This connects your algebraic work with the epistemic theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Zero as structurally equivalent to an empty requirement gap (Delta_t=empty) rather than numerical zero, explicitly connecting the algebraic Zero research line to the epistemic Delta_t/Sat theory just extensively audited in this same batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t). H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}. current candidate operation nucleus includes ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE. But importantly, these are not all canonically frozen as the final minimal operation set. Operation minimality remains an open research problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the state-evolution transition formula and history-append formula, listing a five-operation candidate nucleus (ASSERT/LINK/REVISE/RETRACT/ISOLATE) while explicitly flagging operation minimality as an open research problem, not a frozen final set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not adopt the simplistic rule P, not-P => everything. Instead, contradiction is represented and isolated. real knowledge systems routinely contain conflicting observations, competing hypotheses, outdated information, incompatible sources, different contextual truths. So contradiction is an epistemic state to manage, not a reason to destroy the entire knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS's explicit rejection of classical explosion (P, not-P => everything) in favor of representing and isolating contradiction as a manageable epistemic state, motivated by five named real-world sources of conflicting information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status table (15 rows): K_t as epistemic state RESOLVED/RATIFIED; Reality!=knowledge state ESTABLISHED; Evidence!=truth ESTABLISHED; Truth!=determination!=decision ADOPTED/FOUNDATIONAL; Contradiction/non-explosion RESOLVED/ADOPTED; Representation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Inquiry semantics DEVELOPED; Proposition semantics DEVELOPED; Evidence semantics DEVELOPED; Transformation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Universal Knowledge Algebra NOT ESTABLISHED; Canonical minimal operations OPEN RESEARCH; Complete F4 Sat(K_t,r) semantics NOT ESTABLISHED; Universal semantic equivalence r1 equiv_sem r2 NOT ESTABLISHED; F3<->F4 semantic bridge OPEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a comprehensive fifteen-item status table for the whole theory, distinguishing resolved/established/adopted foundations from explicitly open items (universal Knowledge Algebra, canonical minimal operations, complete F4 Sat semantics, universal equiv_sem, F3<->F4 bridge), the last three matching exactly the open items just extensively audited in this same batch's F4/Model-B series.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The existence and role of Sat are present in the historical corpus, but a fully operational, corpus-native definition of Sat(K_t,r) has not yet been recovered. The later Sat* construction is therefore a candidate construction, not proof that the corpus already contained that exact semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Directly cross-references and restates the same-day F4/Model-B audit series' central finding (S2888-S2897): Sat's existence/role are corpus-present but its full operational semantics are not recovered, and Sat* remains a candidate construction rather than recovered corpus semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not design what the corpus has not established. Where the corpus is insufficient, the correct result is NOT ESTABLISHED / RESEARCH REQUIRED, not an invented definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing methodological rule underlying the whole KnowledgeOS research programme: never design what the corpus has not established; an insufficient corpus should yield the honest classification NOT ESTABLISHED/RESEARCH REQUIRED rather than an invented definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t | Sat(K_t,r)=0}. Therefore Delta_t=empty is the KnowledgeOS notion of Zero Gap. Zero means that there are no unsatisfied requirements remaining within the defined requirement set and satisfaction semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the core Zero-Gap definition as Delta_t=empty over the requirement set R_t and satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r), consistent with the F4/Model-B and kr-rep-reduction lines already covered in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0 != empty in general. Numerical zero means a quantity has value zero. KnowledgeOS Zero is closer to: empty residual requirement set.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes numerical zero from KnowledgeOS Zero (an empty residual requirement set), a set-theoretic rather than quantitative notion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is always relative to the defined requirement/inquiry scope. ... Zero Gap != Complete Knowledge. It means only: There is no remaining gap with respect to the requirements currently being evaluated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against conflating Zero Gap with Complete Knowledge or Complete Reality: satisfying all requirements in a scoped requirement set says nothing about knowledge outside that scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the same K_t can be Zero relative to R_t while simultaneously being Non-zero relative to a larger R'_t. This makes Zero inquiry- and contract-relative, rather than absolute.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing the identical knowledge state K_t can simultaneously be Zero (empty gap) relative to a smaller requirement set and non-Zero relative to a larger superset, establishing Zero as inherently inquiry- and contract-relative rather than an absolute property of K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If a transformation T removes irrelevant information while preserving everything needed to answer the inquiry, then the resulting representation may still have the same gap: Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t). If the gap was already empty, then a valid inquiry-preserving transformation can maintain Delta(T(K_t))=empty. So Zero can function as a preserved semantic condition, not merely as a terminal numerical value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects Zero to the transformation/preservation theory: an inquiry-preserving transformation T maintains the gap Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t), so an already-empty gap remains empty under valid transformations, framing Zero as a preserved semantic condition across the reduction/elimination research family.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, where the subscript reminds us that Zero depends on the relevant requirements R and contract/context C. This is much stronger and safer than saying 'Zero means absence.' It means: There is no unresolved requirement in the specified epistemic task.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest current formulation Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, explicitly parameterized by requirements R and contract/context C, as a safer and stronger statement than an unparameterized 'Zero means absence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: the full operational semantics of Sat(K_t,r) is not yet completely established, especially in the historical F4/Model-B work we just discussed. Therefore Delta_t=empty is theoretically meaningful, but we cannot yet claim that every real KnowledgeOS implementation can compute Zero correctly. Zero definition != Zero computation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-applies the same day's F4/Model-B audit finding (Sat(K_t,r)'s operational semantics not yet established) to the Zero-Gap concept itself, distinguishing Zero definition (theoretically meaningful) from Zero computation (not currently guaranteed correct in any real implementation).

b_rows_sample.statement: Formal before/repair/after test of the 230->232 closure repair against the Reconciliation Gate's 9 required properties: only closure is repaired (Policy added, time re-handled as a sequence index); well-typedness, totality, determinism, composability (Step 232 itself proves T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G), computability, minimality, independence, and historical continuity ALL remain unresolved -- the repair is REAL but PARTIAL, fixing exactly one of nine properties, vindicating the earlier warning that 'a repair that makes a definition larger is not automatically a successful repair'.

b_rows_sample.statement: The decisive convergence finding: three independent methods (executed regex over 182 sources finding I*={Provenance}; executed role-comparison finding Provenance in only 5/9 kernels, absent from BOTH current kernels 230v1 and 232v2; and the formal counterexample showing L=History(T) fails to derive external provenance at t=0) converge on the sharpest structural finding of the reconciliation gate: the history's only universal invariant is absent from the kernel claiming to reconstruct that history, and the argument for its absence (L=History(T)) does not itself hold.

b_rows_sample.statement: Final 4-class verdict per the gate's own mandated schema: (A) ESTABLISHED -- 9 kernels exist with 27/36 competing pairs, two disjoint never-reconciled lineages, Step 232's two incommensurable structures, the partial closure repair, transformation as the sole near-universal primitive, Provenance as I* yet absent from both current kernels; (B) PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS -- L=History(T) holds for internal lineage only; (C) PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED -- the two lineages COULD be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy mappings, explicitly labeled the verifier's own unestablished conjecture, proposed by no corpus document; (D) REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIED -- 070's minimality (REFUTED via TV-F-043), 230/232's minimality (UNPROVEN), mathbb K's well-typedness (UNDER-SPECIFIED), kernel independence (REFUTED for both 230 and 232), and 'one evolving theory' itself (REFUTED -- two competing lineages).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A session assignment is a role-bound assignment in a governed work item ... The physical terminal/process is irrelevant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a 'session = fixed terminal forever' mental model: sessions are role-bound assignments within a governed work item, so one terminal can execute whichever assignment the authoritative workflow record currently authorizes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HANDOFF ≠ ACTIVE / HUMAN START + HANDOFF = ACTIVE
a_rows_sample.statement: States 'no role activates itself' as a central architectural principle: every role follows REGISTERED → (predecessor HANDOFF) → CREATED → (human START) → ACTIVE → HANDOFF/STOP/COMPLETE, with no prose or prompt able to substitute for the mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture is activated by a genuine architectural need, not by a fixed workflow position.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the KOS-OQ-001 precedent (Session 4/Architecture was correctly never activated because Governance determined no architectural work was required) to argue Architecture is conditional, not a fixed sequential step.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A session can know how to perform something without being authorized to perform it ... S3 role + S3 ACTIVE + mutation ownership + implementation grant + scope match = authorized mutation
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates capability (knowing how) from authority (being permitted), formalizing an authorized-mutation condition as the conjunction of role, active state, mutation ownership, an implementation grant, and scope match.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance A — Intake/Authorization ... Governance B — Routing/Registration ... Governance C — Closure
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Governance from a single 'gatekeeper' step into three distinct responsibilities occurring at multiple points in the lifecycle: intake/authorization, routing/registration of the next role, and closure/registration of the final qualification decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not ask Session 4 to design this now. We're still inside the OQ whose purpose is to prove the existing mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refuses to let the desired future capability (automatic session/role discovery) be designed inside the currently-running operational qualification, to avoid contaminating the qualification being measured; assigns it to a new, separately-governed work item routed through Governance→Architecture→Implementation→Verification.

a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: the corpus's own role-model proposals and its own external-research critique of role-first modeling coexist unreconciled.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## How this template must be filled

1. **Sections 6.5 and 6.6 are the blocking pair.** Nothing downstream of them can be completed
   first; several other sections' empty slots (invariant obligations, replay semantics, failure
   semantics) are empty *because* 6.5 is empty.
2. **A section is filled by a governance act, not by a good argument.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Operation Registry (section 6.5) and Transformation Algebra (section 6.6) as the 'blocking pair': both are rated NOT ESTABLISHED, and several other sections' fields (invariant-obligations in 6.4, replay semantics in 6.9, failure semantics in 6.6 itself) are empty specifically BECAUSE 6.5 is empty, making this pair the root cause of the wider implementation-contract emptiness rather than one gap among many; states the governing rule that a section is filled only by a governance act (ratification), never merely by a sound derivation, and that the book documents this contract but never authors it.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## 6.8 Governance / authority model — status: **PARTIAL, with an open collision**

```
  authority as a constraint    —   [canon: precondition filled via governance, never a processing step]
  authority ≠ evidential truth —   [canon: I-4]
  the boundary-crossing act    —   [canon: A6]
  decision contract            —   [canon: DC 6-tuple]
  admissibility conjunction over exactly those 6 —   [MISSING — registered]
  authority → gate binding     —   [MISSING]
  authority-act object         —   [NOT ESTABLISHED in canon]
  ...
  ⚠ policy-loop termination    —   [OPEN: two unreconciled resolutions stand — GC-1]
b_rows_sample.statement: The Governance/Authority Model template section (6.8) is rated PARTIAL with an open collision: canon fixes authority-as-a-precondition-constraint, authority-not-equal-to-evidential-truth (I-4), the Accepted->Committed boundary-crossing act (A6), and the Decision Contract 6-tuple shape, but has no admissibility conjunction over exactly those six fields, no authority-to-gate binding, no typed authority-act object, and the GC-1 policy-loop termination remains open with two unreconciled resolutions standing.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
> **The ratified canon defines when a transition would be ILLEGAL without ever defining what a
> transition IS.**

Two legality constraints are ratified — **I-12** ... and **A6** ... Both constrain a transition relation that the canon never specifies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central finding: the ratified canon defines two legality CONSTRAINTS on state transitions (I-12, the ladder's covering relation excluding skipped moves; A6, that only an authority act, never evidence volume, crosses the Accepted->Committed boundary) without ever defining what a transition itself IS (no signature, no legality condition, no pre/post-conditions); a law quantifying over an undefined relation is not executable, so 'legal transition rules' reach 'ratified' status only as constraints, never as executable semantics.

b_rows_sample.statement: A textual search finds zero occurrences of the strings 'postcondition' or 'post-condition' anywhere in the model/ or final-architecture/ directories of the ratified corpus, while 'precondition' occurs exactly once, describing Authorization's conceptual role (COMPOSITION grade) rather than serving as any specific operation's precondition; preservation obligations and rejection/invalid-transition semantics are both found NOT ESTABLISHED (no artifact maps any operation to invariants it must preserve, and no typed rejection vocabulary -- structural vs policy vs authority refusal -- exists despite the Decision Contract 6-tuple implicitly needing one).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## D · Status declaration

```
Transformations = BLOCKED / NOT CANONICAL
Blocked behind:  the operation registry (primary)
                 state identity + equality (secondary)
                 a closed invariant register (secondary)
```
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally declares Transformations = BLOCKED/NOT CANONICAL, and identifies three specific dependency reasons this cannot be filled in isolation: (1) primary -- a transformation contract is written per-operation, and with zero ratified operations there is nothing to write contracts for, so Transformations is blocked BEHIND Operations, not merely alongside it; (2) secondary -- a postcondition is a predicate over the resulting state, which cannot be checked until K1=K2 is decidable, and canon defines neither identity nor equality; (3) secondary -- 'preserves invariant I-n' presupposes the set of I-n is closed, but canon asserts twelve invariants without asserting that is all of them.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## A · Capabilities the ratified canon REQUIRES but does not define

... | C-1 | move an item one rung up the ladder | ladder + **I-12** | **NO** | yes — layer 2, unratified |
...
**Nine capabilities are canonically required. Zero operations are canonically defined.** That
sentence is the whole gap.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies nine capabilities (C-1..C-9) that the ratified canon logically requires to exist, each traced to a specific ratified forcing element, for none of which is an actual operation defined: C-1 move a ladder rung up (I-12); C-2 attach Committed to an Accepted item by authority act (A6, I-4); C-3 make a Determination Supported->Accepted under AcceptancePolicy (v0.1 concept row, grade READ); C-4 change an in-force policy version via governed decision (I-11, R-1 stratification loop -- GC-1 open); C-5 compose evidence so duplicates don't amplify and corroboration does (I-5, I-6, aggregation operator open by ruling OQ-3); C-6 compute the gap between state and requirement (Zero(K,EC), EC=eta(G,IdealState), R-2); C-7 turn an observation into evidence (the qualification predicate, undefined in canon); C-8 evaluate a decision contract for admissibility (DC 6-tuple, no ratified conjunction over exactly those six); C-9 act and observe the result (the decision interlock, far side open by ruling OQ-4). For every one of the nine, an unratified layer-2 candidate exists outside canon, but none is defined as canon.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
**Reading:** the canon fixes *fragments* — a precondition here, an authority requirement there —
around operations it never defines. Eleven properties × nine capabilities = 99 cells; **9 are
partially fixed by canon, 2 are fully fixed (C-2's authority requirement and its evidence
non-effect), and 88 are empty.** No capability has a complete contract. Not one.
b_rows_sample.statement: A systematic 11-required-property x 9-capability matrix (99 cells: Name, Purpose, Input state, Preconditions, Postconditions, Invariants preserved, Evidence generated/changed, Authority required, Replay semantics, Failure semantics, Ratification status) is filled from the ratified canon only: 9 cells are partially fixed (e.g. C-1/C-2/C-3/C-4 preconditions partially known via I-12/A6/I-11), exactly 2 cells are fully fixed (C-2's authority requirement being YES via A6/I-4, and its evidence-generated field being definitively NONE since evidence cannot cross the boundary per A6), and 88 of 99 cells are entirely empty; the reading is that canon fixes only fragments around operations it never actually defines, so no capability among the nine has a complete contract.
