b_rows_sample.anchor: Three corrections back to the reviewing documents ... "9 rediscoveries, all from unindexed regions" ... REFUTED at n=10 ... "0/11 capabilities are enforcing" ... Objection ... accepted; the substitution loses a distinct finding
b_rows_sample.statement: Three corrections issued back to reviewing documents: (1) 'KnowledgeOS Is the Product' / 'PublicDigit becomes an instance' contradicts AIP-14 and the DA clarification — that is the Vision, not a supported finding; under canon PublicDigit is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; (2) '9 rediscoveries, all from unindexed regions' is refuted at n=10, since occurrence #10 drew on an indexed region named in .claude/CLAUDE.md — the cause is not only a missing index, it is not reading the index that exists; (3) a proposed substitution of '0/11 capabilities enforcing' with 'no capability beyond CAP-001 operationally validated' is rejected as losing a distinct finding — both claims are kept: no capability or check enforces (every one advisory), and no capability beyond CAP-001 has been operationally validated; the enforcement finding matters because knowledgeos init would be the platform's first enforcing mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is the fifth occurrence of a recorded pattern, and the pattern is the most important thing in this document ... Four searches for a missing decision; four decisions already on the record. Five, now
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring pattern is documented at its fifth occurrence: hypotheses that a lifecycle/placement-policy/maturity-structure/product-status/strategic-domain-model is missing, each time already answered by an existing standard (ES-006.1, ES-005.3, ES-005.2+R-37, a DA ruling, and now section 8 of the Reference Model + ES-005.1/.3 + section 7.2 + ES-006.1). The failure mode is procedural: proposing before searching.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What this costs my own prior reports — three corrections ... This is the SIXTH occurrence of the programme's own recorded failure mode — proposing before searching — and the most expensive
b_rows_sample.statement: Three prior claims are refuted by the newly admitted evidence: (1) 'no strategic-DDD method exists' is refuted a second time — there are two complementary methods (Round47-OP's admissible criteria, the R16 Workbook's investigation procedure, including Actor Analysis and Competing Interpretations found only in the workbook); (2) 'no decision-record template exists' is refuted — Round17_ARB_Decision_Record_Template.md is a genuine unfilled template; (3) the Fitness Assessment's 'Strategic Discovery: EVIDENCE n=1' is wrong — Strategic Discovery has an executed 16-round programme behind it (92 artifacts); the n=1 belongs to bootstrap, not to the method. This is recorded as the sixth occurrence of 'proposing before searching' in the programme, including one committed by the same author earlier the same day (re-performing consistency-boundary discovery when Round27D_ARB_Consistency_Boundary_Review.md already existed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE SWEEP FOUND THREE MORE REDISCOVERIES — AND THEY HIT TODAY'S FLAGSHIP DELIVERABLES ... The count rises from 6 to 9
b_rows_sample.statement: Three new rediscoveries are found against the author's own same-day deliverables, raising the programme's rediscovery count from 6 to 9: (7) 'P1' (Method/Binding/Evidence decomposition, presented as new) duplicates Round38C-04_Principle_Form_Classification_Framework (ARB-authorized, classifies ADR elements as Principle/Form/Ambiguous); (8) the Platform Capability Model (25 capabilities) duplicates Platform_Capability_Pattern.md (PROVISIONALLY STABLE, FROZEN, PGP-01..05), which states the same rationale verbatim; (9) a requested 'knowledge taxonomy' duplicates the already-COMPLETE RQ-002_Knowledge_Meta_Model.md.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ROLE CLARIFIED 2026-08-02 ... What is REFUTED: §10's "all nine rediscoveries drew on UNINDEXED regions" correlation. Occurrence #10 drew on an INDEXED region
b_rows_sample.statement: A claim within this same document ('all nine rediscoveries drew on unindexed regions') is refuted at a tenth occurrence: occurrence #10 drew on an indexed region that .claude/CLAUDE.md names explicitly — the cause is not only a missing index, it is also not reading the index that exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Single highest-value knowledge-engineering improvement? AN INDEX OF ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE — keyed to the EXISTING taxonomies, inventing none
b_rows_sample.statement: The single highest-value knowledge-engineering improvement identified is an index of engineering knowledge, keyed to existing taxonomies, inventing none: it is the sole cause behind 9 rediscoveries, needs no ARB ruling/extraction/movement/new governance, and its rate is accelerating (3 of 9 rediscoveries happened the same day this document was written). The cheapest sufficient form is one file listing each instrument, its class, location, and reuse evidence — this document is its first draft.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The governing principle in §1 was written five files before the Kernel boundary act, and the boundary act's adversarial pass still failed to apply it to ConflictRecord -- the HPA had to supply that challenge. The corpus was available and the principle in it was not used. That is an argument for reading corpora before acts, not after.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records a concrete instance of the model-amnesia failure pattern: a governing principle already present in the corpus was not applied to a subsequent architecture act (ConflictRecord) even though it was directly relevant, requiring an external human to supply the challenge -- offered as an argument for reading a corpus before acting on it, not merely after.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'C-1'

a_rows_sample.anchor: M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, sim: epistemic indistinguishability, V: valuation ... KnowledgeState != InquiryState, or more precisely K_t != QState_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads the thesis's core model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (a possible-worlds model with a distinct issue/question relation approx and an epistemic-indistinguishability relation sim) as structural support for KnowledgeState != InquiryState (K_t != QState_t), where K_t is what the system currently represents/attributes and QState_t is what is currently being investigated and which alternatives/questions are active; proposes a richer Inquiry = Question + IssueStructure + EpistemicState + Purpose/Contract in place of a bare tuple Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement -- not as an identity, but as a research hypothesis. ... questioning actions ... do not themselves give information immediately; they raise/manage issues ... almost exactly our ZF5: ZoomIn != FactFinding
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement as a research hypothesis (not identity), and reports that the thesis's characterization of questioning actions as knowledge-seeking actions that do not themselves supply information gives an external theoretical analogue for the already-adopted ZF5 (ZoomIn != FactFinding) and DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is no question composition principle ... sequential questioning can produce structures that cannot be represented by one equivalent question. ... Dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition ... KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the thesis's finding that many apparent composition laws fail for questioning actions (sequence order matters; no general question-composition principle exists) as an external research precedent for taking non-commutativity of KnowledgeOS inquiry operations seriously, connecting to the corpus's own empirical Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) findings, while explicitly refusing to claim the source 'proves' KnowledgeOS non-commutativity ([EXT] dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition -> [PROP] KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define observable/question-relevant behavior first -> define equivalence -> minimize structure. ... That does not solve KnowledgeOS semantic equivalence. But it gives us a very strong research direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts a three-step methodological pattern from the thesis's behavioral-equivalence-then-minimization work (define observable/question-relevant behavior first, then define equivalence, then minimize structure) as a candidate strategy relevant to the corpus's unresolved semantic equivalence (equiv_sem) and capability-preorder (<=_cap) problem, explicitly not itself a solution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... Issue/Knowledge Separation ... Question as State-Changing Object ... Issue Refinement ... Resolution ... Inquiry Composition ... Behavioral Equivalence ... Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with six research questions (issue/knowledge separation; question as state-changing object; issue refinement for Zoom-In; determination as contract-relative issue resolution; inquiry-operation commutativity; question-relative behavioral equivalence contributing to equiv_sem) plus a seventh bridge Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency via the thesis's local-property querying-strategy chapter, all tagged [EXT]/[PROP], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no new primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure ... M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, representing the alternatives currently relevant to investigation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the thesis's central distinction Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure via the model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (possible worlds W, epistemic indistinguishability sim, issue/question relation approx representing alternatives currently relevant to investigation, valuation V), extremely close to the corpus's own emerging Zoom-In problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: soft announcements that cut epistemic links while keeping the whole model available for further reference ... contrasted with eliminative announcements. ... Focus != Delete ... Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's 'soft announcement' operator (cuts epistemic links while keeping the whole model available, contrasted with eliminative announcements) as an established formal precedent closely resembling the corpus's own ZF1 (Focus != Delete, Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction), explicitly not treated as proof of ZF1 within KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question and resolution are different operations ... Question changes the issue structure. Resolution changes the epistemic relation in response to the issue. ... Yes: K_b phi, No: K_b neg phi, Don'tKnow: neg K_b phi and neg K_b neg phi. ... Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's Question != Resolution separation (question changes issue structure, resolution changes the epistemic relation) and its tripartite answer structure (Yes: K_b(phi); No: K_b(not-phi); Don'tKnow: not-K_b(phi) and not-K_b(not-phi), a legitimate epistemic outcome, not an error) as external formal support for the corpus's own ZoomIn!=FactFinding->Determination pipeline and for Question Raised does not imply Knowledge Acquired / Discovery of an Issue does not imply Determination -- described as almost exactly the Case B witness already designed for KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01, while warning not to copy the three-valued structure directly into KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a candidate may be excluded only when the local property provides a justified reason that it cannot be a solution. ... SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion. ... Excludes(h | E,Q,C,S,R) with a warrant for exclusion. ... Zero != SearchPruning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's query-strategy safety condition (a candidate may be excluded from the search space only when a local property provides a justified reason it cannot be a solution) to propose Excludes(h|E,Q,C,S,R) with an explicit exclusion warrant, giving SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion; separates this Query Strategy/SearchPruning question ('which parts of the search space can safely be ignored while preserving the possibility of finding the solution') from the Zero Lens question ('can this structure be eliminated while preserving the contract'), Zero != SearchPruning, with only a possible (not assumed) relation Zero -> Safe Reduction -> Query Strategy under a suitable contract.

type_signature.domain: hypothesis h, evidence E, inquiry Q, context C, standard S, regime R

a_rows_sample.anchor: ordinary bisimulation was insufficient ... developed a richer behavioral equivalence -- intersection bisimulation/intersimulation -- to preserve exactly the distinctions relevant to the language. ... Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it. ... Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's discovery that ordinary bisimulation was insufficient (it could erase strategically relevant information while preserving modal truth) and its development of a richer intersimulation/intersection-bisimulation equivalence, as a concrete formal precedent for the corpus's unresolved equiv_sem problem and kernel-minimality programme (Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it), giving Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation and Observable equivalence depends on what the observer/contract can observe, reinforcing 'minimality is semantic, not syntactic.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which source should be queried? ... different information sources, including agents and objective sources/oracles ... SourceSelection != FactFinding. It is an agency/query-planning decision. ... query-available information can be limited by subjective knowledge, measurement instruments, experimental design, computing power, missing resources ... Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's source-selection and resource-limitation discussion to propose S_t^available={Human,Log,Instrument,Database,Network,Agent,Oracle,...} and SelectSource(Q,K,C,S,R), giving SourceSelection != FactFinding (an agency/query-planning decision) and connecting resource limitations (subjective knowledge, instruments, computing power) to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Why' questions concern reasons for behavior ... What? -> How? -> Why? -> Why act? ... The last question is already Action Warrant. So this thesis gives additional support for our F_t != W_t != Decision_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's identification of 'why' questions (concerning reasons for behavior) as external support connecting to the corpus's Action Fact-Finding work: a What?->How?->Why?->Why-act? hierarchy where the last question is already Action Warrant, reinforcing F_t != W_t != Decision_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a realistic inquiry does not merely contain an unordered set of questions. It maintains a structured agenda whose issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted. ... Inquiry_t = structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's structured-inquiry-agenda concept (issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted; being good at research includes asking good questions, not only answering them) to propose Inquiry_t as a structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues rather than a single question Q_t, and recursive sub-question generation Q_0->Q_1,...,Q_n with Q_i->E_i->Q_{i+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = <Q_t, approx_t, D_t^cand, S_t^source, A_t> ... Factivity Separation: I_t carries no truth assertions ... Non-Destructive Focus: Focus(I_t,w) not-implies w not-in K_t ... State Evolution Autonomy: Delta I_t != empty not-implies Delta K_t != empty (Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the candidate Inquiry State schema I_t=(Q_t,approx_t,D_t^cand,S_t^source,A_t) (active question DAG with per-question id/target/status/priority; issue-partitioning relation approx_t over states; candidate dimension set; source-dependency map; inquiry agenda/history) with three explicit separation rules: Factivity Separation (I_t carries no truth assertions), Non-Destructive Focus (focusing does not remove states from K_t), and State Evolution Autonomy (Delta I_t!=empty does not imply Delta K_t!=empty), giving ZF5 a clean formal witness Delta I_t!=empty AND Delta K_t=empty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: (K_t,I_t,O_t) -> (I_{t+1}, D^cand_{t+1}) ... K_t: Current frozen Epistemic State (Unmutated). ... KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... DQ1 ... DQ5 ... Does KnowledgeOS require a distinct evolving Inquiry State in order to model fact-finding correctly?
a_rows_sample.statement: Finalizes the ZoomIn operational interface as ZoomIn:(K_t,I_t,O_t)->(I_{t+1},D^cand_{t+1}) leaving K_t unmutated, with a five-step execution sequence (trigger binding, issue-structure restructuring via soft update, candidate dimension discovery, agenda/sub-question generation, source-dependency assignment feeding downstream FactFinding); registers KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with DQ1-DQ5 (is a dedicated I_t strictly required; how do soft issue updates re-partition alternatives without destroying context; can safe candidate pruning be bounded by exclusion warrants; how does intersimulation bound equiv_sem minimality; how should hierarchical agendas manage recursive sub-questions); poses the deeper research question of whether KnowledgeOS requires a distinct evolving Inquiry State to model fact-finding correctly, while explicitly keeping KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 as the sole active experiment and using this thesis only as an interpretive lens for its results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The attached book is not Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction. It is Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis, Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry. The file itself identifies that title and author... The previous Sher attribution should therefore not be carried forward for this file.
a_rows_sample.statement: Self-declared source-attribution correction (extracted here as a claim, per the corpus's standing rule that self-declared statuses require independent verification rather than acceptance on citation): the volume most recently analyzed in the preceding thread, previously attributed to Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction, is stated to actually be Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry, identified from the file's own title page and Chapter 2 heading; the prior Sher attribution is explicitly withdrawn for this file going forward.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R = sim intersect approx ... What remains possible when we consider both what the agent cannot distinguish and what the current issue considers relevant. ... this intersection is not reducible to either relation alone. ... A_t^rel = A_t^epi intersect A_t^issue.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's intersection relation R=sim∩approx (what remains possible given both epistemic indistinguishability and current issue relevance, not reducible to either relation alone) as inspiration for a candidate A_t^rel=A_t^epi ∩ A_t^issue representing currently relevant epistemic alternatives that must actually be investigated, tagged [PROP].

a_rows_sample.anchor: Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined ... A gap is not necessarily simply 'something missing.' It can be an unresolved issue over a structured set of alternatives. ... Issue(Q,K_t) = partition/distinction structure over admissible alternatives.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts a four-way separation Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined from the thesis's formulas distinguishing facts neither known nor settled that would become known upon resolution, warning that the corpus's existing Gap concept risks carrying too much responsibility (a gap can be an unresolved issue over a structured alternative set, not merely 'something missing'), proposing Issue(Q,K_t) as a candidate partition/distinction structure, [PROP] only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Questioning != Answering != Resolution which translates very naturally into: ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination. This is one of the strongest external correspondences we have found so far. But it remains [EXT] -> [PROP], not [PROVED].
a_rows_sample.statement: States that Minica's Questioning != Answering != Resolution translates naturally into ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination, describing it as the strongest external correspondence found so far for ZF5, explicitly kept at [EXT]->[PROP], not [PROVED]; separately notes Issue Refinement != Information Elimination reinforces the triad ZoomIn != Zero != FactFinding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minica explicitly demonstrates that many apparently intuitive composition laws for question/announcement actions do not hold... there is no general question-composition principle for the richer system. ... phi?;phi? != phi? in general. ... we explicitly decided not to assume projection properties for Zoom-In. So the book independently reinforces that decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's demonstration that composition and iteration are not automatically well-behaved for questioning/announcement actions (sequential compositions are not generally equivalent under swap; asking the same question twice need not equal asking it once, phi?;phi? != phi? in general) as independent external reinforcement of the corpus's own methodological rule (do not infer algebraic laws from intuitive operator meaning; test composition explicitly) and of the earlier decision not to assume idempotence/projection properties for Zoom-In, connecting to the corpus's own Zero(S1) and Zero(S2) not implying Zero(S1 union S2) finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At every observation you have infinite possible dimensions to be discovered. ... the projection to different observation field by zooming in can be the fact finding process about an event or process
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that at every observation there is a potentially unbounded discoverable dimension space, and that zooming into different observation fields to find causes/situations/sources of an event constitutes the fact-finding process about that event, using a Nexus egress=70GB/day example with potentially relevant dimensions {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,GitLabRunner,Configuration,Users,Traffic,Logs,Storage,Time,Security,Deployment,...}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_t subseteq D* and potentially D* -> open/unbounded discovery space. ... Don't claim literally that the dimensions are mathematically infinite unless the model establishes such a domain. Instead: the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the informal 'infinite possible dimensions' claim to a precise formulation: the currently represented dimensions D_t are a subset of a potentially discoverable D*, and the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation (D_t -Inquiry-> D_{t+1}), without D_{t+1} necessarily being a superset of D_t since dimensions can also become irrelevant/superseded/out-of-contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q) -> FocusedInquirySpace ... The dimensions explored by Zoom-in need not have been present in the original observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Zoom-in from the earlier K_t->Subgraph(K_t) (found inadequate) to ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q)->FocusedInquirySpace, where focus is not deletion of the rest of K_t and the explored dimensions need not have been present in the original observation -- a discovery operation rather than a within-representation detail operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Graph Traversal != Epistemic Investigation ... KnowledgeGraph = representational substrate ... ZoomIn = inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates Graph Traversal (a Knowledge Graph can represent an edge like GitLabRunner-causes->Egress) from Epistemic Investigation (KnowledgeOS asks why the edge should exist, requiring Evidence, Provenance, Time, AlternativeHypotheses, Assessment, Determination), giving KnowledgeGraph=representational substrate while ZoomIn=inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t) = Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t) rather than simply FocusedState -> OriginalState. ... this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled: we were trying to classify Zoom-out before clearly separating restoration from integration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).

b_rows_sample.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should be built around Pramana (Knowledge Sources), not Knowledge Objects... Knowledge is not primarily a stored thing. Knowledge is the output of a reliable process.
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a modern Data->Information->Knowledge model with a Nyaya-inspired Object->Knowledge Source(Pramana)->Valid Cognition->Successful Action pipeline, arguing this book gives 'the runtime architecture of epistemic operations' as opposed to the prior book's 'logic of justification'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: pramana = process/source, prameya = object known, pramatr = knower, pramiti = knowledge/cognition. The four must be correctly related for truth to be grasped.
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the four-part pramana/prameya/pramatr/pramiti relation onto a KnowledgeEvent YAML schema (knower/object/source/cognition/validity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nyaya does not ask: 'Does this belief have a justification?' It asks: 'Was this cognition generated by a reliable knowledge-producing process?'... contrasts Nyaya with internalist Western epistemology
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Nyaya is process-reliabilist rather than internalist-justificationist, contrasting an LLM pattern ('Generate answer -> Hope it is correct') with a proposed KnowledgeOS pattern ('Generate claim -> Identify production process -> Check process reliability -> Accept/reject knowledge').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Source Registry ... perception: reliability: high_for: [infrastructure_state, runtime_metrics] ... The book identifies four knowledge sources: perception, inference, analogy, testimony
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes adding a 'Pramana Registry' / Knowledge Source Registry with a YAML schema recording per-source reliability conditions, alongside existing Evidence/Observations/Decisions/ADRs/Governance records.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Confidence State Machine: OBSERVED -> INFERRED -> ACCEPTED -> CHALLENGED -> UNDER REVIEW -> VALIDATED / REJECTED. Not every fact needs an expensive review.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'Epistemic Escalation', a knowledge-confidence state machine with six states, explicitly to avoid the cost of reviewing every fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS becomes an Epistemic Operating System... Epistemic Governance Layer -> Knowledge Production Engine [Observation, Inference, Testimony] -> Validation Engine -> Knowledge Objects -> Action / Decision

a_rows_sample.statement: Grants: a grant without a humanActRef is refused by the engine ('the record never manufactures authority -- G-2/R5b'). Exactly one mutation owner per work item is mechanically enforced (I-1). Closure is a governance act (G-1): COMPLETE refuses any writer but governance/human. Producer != acceptor (R-34, INV-ATTR-2): a process cannot verify/accept its own work; separation is declared, not attestable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-3 ... AST-019's implementing session held no registered lane on this work item, and its runtime identity is recorded nowhere by UUID ... the producer bar for AST-019's future verification is not mechanically enforceable -- there is no recorded producer identity to exclude
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a governance-model gap: because AST-019's implementing session never registered a lane or recorded its runtime identity, the producer-verifier separation principle cannot be mechanically enforced for its future verification (no producer identity exists to exclude), and the operating model as written has no lane-shape at all for a human-authorized amendment slice landing on a STOPPED work item.

a_rows_sample.anchor: sixteen barred identities means the eligible pool is nearly exhausted. The 'genuinely fresh session' requirement is now load-bearing rather than ceremonial -- it is the only remaining way to field a verifier at all.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observes that the accumulating list of barred identities across this multi-step governance saga has grown to 16 entries, to the point that the requirement for a genuinely fresh session (rather than any reused process) has become the sole remaining mechanism for fielding an eligible verifier at all -- recorded as a one-occurrence observation, not promoted to a general rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Using an unverified capability to manufacture the authority to verify that capability makes the verification worthless. A PASS would rest on the subject's own correctness -- the thing in question.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the circularity bar as a general governance principle: a candidate must never use the very capability it is appointed to verify (or any unauthorized capability) to manufacture its own activation, because doing so would make the eventual verification verdict rest on the subject's own unproven correctness -- self-identified independently by the candidate before any instruction forbade it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the author of the defect does not rule on its remedy. ... Recovery determination -- recommend A, on grounds, not convenience ... R-34/EP-02: the author of the defect does not rule on its remedy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the producer-verifier separation principle (R-34/EP-02) to defect remediation: the process that authored a governance defect may analyze it fully and recommend a remedy with grounds, but must not itself decide which recovery path (proceed with documented defect vs. discard and re-appoint) is taken -- that decision is reserved for the PO/ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: re-verification by a process that is NOT 84c0f6f6 (first verifier), NOT 1899d8bf (producer), NOT 5928b9f9 (this governance process) ... Step 3 is where the ASD-001 lesson is spent. The appointment for the repair slice must go through AST-018 appoint
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a full governed repair sequence (human CONTINUATION -> fresh implementation candidate declaration -> Governance appoints THROUGH the appointment engine, explicitly not hand-composed as in ASD-001 -> human START -> EP-01 plan approval -> RED/GREEN -> re-verification by a fourth process excluded from all three prior roles -> separate PO/ARB adoption+authorization decisions), directly applying the ASD-001 lesson by requiring the repair's own appointment go through the canonical engine this time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence must be declared and assessed on PRIOR PARTICIPATION, not on identity difference. A different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence. ... A restarted process is a new candidate until Governance explicitly establishes its participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the corollary that carries the load: independence must be assessed on disclosed prior participation, never merely on identity difference, since a different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of true independence; the resulting safe rule is that a restarted process is treated as a new candidate until Governance explicitly re-establishes its participation, explicitly rejecting as dangerous the alternative of treating UUIDs as durable, permanent identities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That process authored ASD-001, scoped REPAIR-001, recorded the CONTINUATION (seq 5) and the grant G-REPAIR-001, and wrote the candidate-declaration prompt. Appointing it would collapse the separation between Governance analysis and Implementation ... The mechanism would not have caught this. AST-018 appoint might well have accepted e40f3fd0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms O-5's abstract danger with a concrete live instance: the governance-recording process that scoped and authorized REPAIR-001 reappeared under a new runtime identifier (e40f3fd0) after a restart, which appears on no identity bar list, so the mechanical appointment check (AST-018 appoint) would have accepted it as independent -- the bar had to be applied manually by the PO/ARB on participation grounds since the mechanism itself would not have caught it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process added itself to the implementer bar the moment it recorded §2-§6. Governance-recording is not a lane, but it is participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a process recording a governance decision, though holding no formal workflow lane, is itself a participation act that self-bars that process from later filling an independence-sensitive role on the same matter -- governance-recording capacity is explicitly not exempt from participation-based exclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(kos, ai, "Bootstraps and constrains AI sessions") Rel(ai, kos, "Executes assigned work under grants")
b_rows_sample.statement: The KnowledgeOS system bootstraps and constrains AI sessions, and the AI/Agent Runtime executes assigned work under grants -- a two-directional relation between the governed platform and executing AI sessions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Component(workflow, "Workflow Engine", "Governed workflow", "Grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions")
b_rows_sample.statement: The Workflow Engine component is defined as owning grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions -- the governed-workflow mechanism later referred to throughout the batch as BC-7 / the workflow-state engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(review, verification, "Routes independent verification")
b_rows_sample.statement: A Review Engine component is proposed whose role is to route independent verification and preserve role separation, distinct from the Verification Engine component itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContainerDb(estate, "Knowledge / Workflow Estate", "Git + governed records", "Architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests")
b_rows_sample.statement: A single durable 'Knowledge / Workflow Estate' store (git + governed records) is proposed as the persistence layer for architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture lane S4 was HANDED_OFF at seq 5 and NEVER returned to ACTIVE
b_rows_sample.statement: Programmatic check of the workflow record shows the architecture lane producing Amendment 1 held mutation ownership at HANDOFF but never received a START/CONTINUATION afterward, meaning Amendment 1 was produced by a lane not verifiably ACTIVE on the record -- distinguished from whether its claims are independently assessable (they are).

b_rows_sample.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
b_rows_sample.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: this verification lane has no START on the record, so this report is produced off-record, the second occurrence at the "Verification #3" slot in this estate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding X-2: this verification's own workflow lane has no recorded START, meaning the report is produced off-record -- the second occurrence of the same lifecycle-gap pattern at a 'Verification #3' slot across this estate, classified as a platform gap (bearing on C-10/knowledge-distribution and G-3) rather than a defect of Correction #2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Correction #2 finished its work and said so in the artifact, but its lane never handed off -- it still held mutation ownership when this act arrived.
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring delivery/record gap pattern is recorded: an artifact states it is delivered, but the lane that produced it never performed the corresponding HANDOFF transition, so the workflow record lags the actual work; Governance performs the handoff now rather than back-dating it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X-2 is a live blocker ... the work item's mutationOwner is None: seq 14 handed off to a lane that then never STARTed, so ownership was released and never taken up. Consequently no lane can hand off
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow lane that is HANDED_OFF to but never STARTed leaves mutationOwner as None, mechanically blocking every subsequent lane's handoff (Inv C requires the current mutation owner to hand off) -- a live, measured blocker rather than a theoretical one, confirmed by probing a scratch copy of the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option A -- transcribing the missing START -- is not available to Governance. A transcription records a human act that was given. No such act exists in this lane's record, and Governance may not supply one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance determines it cannot itself transcribe a missing human START act, because a transcription records a fact (that a human act occurred) which only the PO/ARB can supply; Governance instead retains the report as evidence produced off-record, leaving option A open to the PO/ARB at any time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: restoring append-only history is itself a history edit, two lanes were writing this file the same day, and a restoration performed without authority would repeat the very defect it repairs.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to restore 73 deleted lines from an append-only session log, reasoning that restoring append-only history is itself a history-edit and could repeat the defect it would fix; it instead recommends preserving current history with an explicit recovery-commit pointer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The record is not broken. It is exactly ONE HUMAN ACT short.
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagnosis: the entire workflow chain is blocked by exactly one missing human START act; once the PO/ARB affirms it occurred, Governance transcribes the START (preserving on the record's face that the artifact predates the transition) and the blocked handoff chain unblocks in one move.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is an important distinction between the role model and the workflow state machine. The roles tell us who may act; the lifecycle tells us what happens and in what order.
b_rows_sample.statement: A foundational distinction is drawn between the role model (who may act) and the workflow state machine (what happens and in what order), presented as two separate but related layers of the governed AI engineering lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A deliverable being produced is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: A critical rule surfaced from the BC-7 history: a deliverable being produced (content exists) is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed (the governed record reflects it) -- the earliest statement in this batch of the delivery/record gap pattern that recurs dozens of times in later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A lane cannot hand off work the record does not show it ever started. ... Governance will not manufacture the START, and will not record the bootstrap form from: null
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance refuses a directed HANDOFF because the predecessor lane, though it produced a delivered artifact, was never STARTed on the record and therefore holds no mutation ownership; refuses both manufacturing a START and using a null-predecessor bootstrap form, because either would falsely assert something about the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the START sits at seq 25, later in the log than the work it authorized. This is recorded deliberately and is not an error to be tidied ... no historical ordering is invented
b_rows_sample.statement: A governance transcription convention is established: when a human act is confirmed after the fact, its transition is recorded at its true (later) sequence position, not back-dated to appear before the work it authorized -- the record states explicitly that the artifact predates the transcription.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A later act is not automatically a supersession. Act B may be an amendment superseding Act A, a re-issue that crossed with it, or a duplicate. ... Until Governance disposes, a0b61305 remains the recorded DECIDED text
b_rows_sample.statement: A general governance principle: a later act arriving on an already-DECIDED slot is not automatically read as superseding it; until Governance explicitly disposes of the relationship (amendment, re-issue, or duplicate), the earlier recorded DECIDED text remains authoritative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: acts and records have crossed four times -- seq-16 and seq-22 transcriptions, the seq-21 producer designation, the S4b missing START, and now two D1 acts.
b_rows_sample.statement: A cumulative pattern is named explicitly: the record and the governed acts on this work item have crossed (diverged and required reconciliation) four separate times, treated as a recurring structural pattern each disposed individually by Governance rather than absorbed silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Handing off from S5 would set S5 to HANDED_OFF, misrepresenting an OUTSTANDING verification as concluded. ... a lane with no recorded handoff can never legally START. ... Registering an assignment now would create a permanently unreachable lane.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to register a new workflow lane for D5, because the current mutation owner (S5, an outstanding/refused verification) would need to hand off, which would misrepresent that verification as concluded; instead D5 proceeds as a PO/ARB-directed act, deferring the lane-creation question until S5's disposition is settled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HANDED_OFF means the lane RELEASED MUTATION OWNERSHIP. It does NOT mean the verification was performed. a lane that refused on independence now reads, in the state column, indistinguishably from lanes that finished their work.
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow-engine state-vocabulary risk is named: the HANDED_OFF state denotes only that mutation ownership was released, not that any verification, consumption, or acceptance occurred -- so a lane that refused on independence grounds becomes indistinguishable, in the raw state column, from a lane that actually finished its work, requiring explicit clarification for any later reader.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem (Closure and Structural Completeness): ... R_req is structurally complete if and only if every minimal information requirement I(tau) for all tau in T is mapped to a non-collapsing partition in R_req. Proof Construction (By Information-Theoretic Partitioning): 1. Sufficiency ... 2. Minimality ... 3. Closure: R_req is closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations.
a_rows_sample.statement: States and sketches a proof for a Structural Completeness Theorem for R_req: R_req is structurally complete iff every minimal information requirement of every minimal operational task (contradiction isolation, Zero-state checking, epistemic query resolution, temporal garbage collection) maps to a non-collapsing partition. The proof construction has three parts: Sufficiency (append any distinction found missing by a task-output divergence), Minimality (keep only distinctions with a witnessing test vector), and Closure (R_req closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations, sim_{d_i AND d_j} = sim_{d_i} intersect sim_{d_j}).

type_signature.domain: task set T and distinction set R_req

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-1.3 Explicit vs. Implicit Knowledge ... Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi. Tractability: O(1) for explicit; NP-hard in general for implicit deduction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds D-1.3 Explicit-vs-Implicit Knowledge to the R_req inventory (Tier P1): Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi; explicit lookup is O(1), implicit deduction is NP-hard in general -- connecting this batch's FR-1/K^exp-K^der distinction into the R_req formal distinction inventory with a stated complexity class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-5.1 Analytic vs. Synthetic Truth ... D-5.2 Necessary vs. Contingent Modality ... Necessary (Box phi), Contingent (Diamond phi and Diamond not-phi) ... Kripke frame accessibility valuation ... PSPACE-complete in general modal logics; approximated via static metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds two new Tier P2 distinctions to R_req: D-5.1 Analytic (true by definition/tautology) vs Synthetic (true by empirical observation); D-5.2 Necessary (Box phi) vs Contingent (Diamond phi and Diamond not-phi) modality via Kripke-frame accessibility valuation, noting general modal-logic decision is PSPACE-complete but approximated here via static metadata annotation rather than full modal inference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Integration with Contr ... When two incoming streams present e1 |- P and e2 |- not-P: 1. Contr sets KnowledgeStatus(P) = Contradictory (B={T,F} in FDE). 2. It prevents total logical explosion by trapping the assertion within an isolated contradiction frame. 3. It initializes ResolutionStatus(P) = Unresolved. 4. If d in R_req were collapsed, Contr would either trigger classical explosion or falsely collapse the state into Unknown.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the required integration between R_req and the Contr contradiction-isolation subsystem: on conflicting evidence e1|-P and e2|-not-P, Contr must set KnowledgeStatus(P)=Contradictory, trap the assertion in an isolated frame to prevent explosion, and initialize ResolutionStatus(P)=Unresolved; explicitly states that collapsing any of D-1.1/D-3.1/D-4.1 would force either classical explosion or a false collapse into Unknown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4.2 Integration with Zero Lens Specification ... 0_KnowledgeOS iff for all P in K: (Status(P) not-in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P) == Current)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Zero-state predicate for KnowledgeOS: 0_KnowledgeOS holds iff every proposition P in K has KnowledgeStatus(P) not in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P)==Current, i.e. no unsatisfied requirements or unhandled contradictions and no stale dependencies; requires all R_req distinctions to remain expressible without loss.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4.3 Integration with Evaluation Engine ... Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum_{d_i in R_req} w_i * I(Collapse(d_i,pi)) ... An adequate kernel projection requires Loss_{R_req}(pi) == 0 for all P1 distinctions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a quantitative Loss function for the Evaluation Engine using R_req as its metric: Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum over d_i in R_req of w_i times an indicator of whether pi collapses d_i, with priority weights w_i (P1=1.0, P2=0.5); an adequate kernel projection must achieve Loss_{R_req}(pi)==0 for every Tier-P1 distinction -- a concrete quantification of the Representation Adequacy principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5. Formal Ratification & Governance Path ... Phase 1: Draft Review & Completeness Proof [COMPLETED] -> Phase 2: Formal Verification & Test Vectors [COMPLETED] -> Phase 3: HPA Supervisory Ratification [CURRENT STAGE] -> Phase 4: Kernel Candidate Adoption Baseline (v1.0 Frozen). Protocol Policies: Immutability of Tier P1 ... Extension Protocol requires ... Two-thirds approval from the HPA Supervisory group.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-phase governance workflow for R_req (Draft Review & Completeness Proof marked COMPLETED, Formal Verification & Test Vectors marked COMPLETED, HPA Supervisory Ratification marked CURRENT STAGE, Kernel Candidate Adoption Baseline v1.0 Frozen as the final phase) plus protocol policies: Tier P1 distinctions are immutable across v1.x, and any new P2/P3 distinction requires a test-vector necessity demonstration, a tractability proof of no P1 regression, and two-thirds HPA Supervisory approval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 6. Ratification Recommendation & Sign-Off ... The supervisory criteria specified in KR-RREQ-2026 Completion Assessment have been fulfilled ... Status Recommendation: RATIFY R_req v1.0 as the binding normative contract for KnowledgeOS Kernel Development.
a_rows_sample.statement: Issues a self-declared recommendation, within the same authoring pass that also asserts the completeness proof and test vectors, to RATIFY R_req v1.0 as the binding normative contract for KnowledgeOS Kernel Development, citing fulfillment of a named 'KR-RREQ-2026 Completion Assessment' criteria list (completeness theorem, extended inventory, tractability analysis, system integrations, governance workflow).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Documents: RREQ-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-1-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-CONTR-v1.0 ... The Governing Insight: R_req is the semantic contract. ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle. ABK-1 achieves 100% compliance across all Tier P1 and P2 distinctions. The Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary frames the package's governing insight: R_req is the semantic contract, ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle achieving claimed 100% compliance across Tier P1/P2, and the Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation -- packaging three previously-separate documents (R_req, ABK-1, ABK-Contr) plus a test-verification document for joint ratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Tier P1 -- Core Invariants (Must Preserve): D-1.1 Knowledge Status, D-1.2 Justification Mode, D-1.3 Explicit vs. Implicit, D-2.1 Currency & Validity, D-3.1 Evidential Directionality, D-3.2 Absence vs. Evidence of Absence ... Tier P2 -- Required: D-1.4, D-2.2, D-4.1, D-4.2 ... Tier P3 -- Deferred: D-5.1, D-5.2, D-5.3
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the condensed 'Ratified Distinction Inventory': six Tier-P1 distinctions (now including D-1.3 Explicit-vs-Implicit as a core invariant, an escalation from its earlier P1/general placement), four Tier-P2 (dropping earlier-seen candidates like de-dicto/de-re and intensional/extensional-as-a-named-P2-item, retaining Intensional-vs-Extensional Identity, Allen Relations, Resolution Status, Boundary/Scope), and three Tier-P3 deferred items (Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a newly-named Deontic/Normative Can-vs-Should distinction) -- 12 distinctions total, matching the ratification-status block's 'Distinction Inventory: COMPLETE (12 distinctions)'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Criterion 3: Zero Compliance: Zero(s) iff for all d in Tier1(R_req), there exists v in V_d such that E(s) represents v
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 'Zero Compliance' verification criterion within R_req itself: Zero(s) holds iff for every Tier-1 distinction d, the encoding E(s) represents some value v of d -- a coverage-style condition (every P1 distinction is assigned some value) distinct from, but feeding, the package's later flat claim that Zero simply equals R_req compliance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VERDICT: READY FOR RATIFICATION. The submitted documents collectively satisfy the three missing components identified in the previous assessment: 1. Completeness argument -- Provided ... 2. Tractability analysis -- Provided ... 3. Ratification path -- Provided
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames itself as a follow-up assessment answering a prior review's finding of three missing components (completeness argument, tractability analysis, ratification path) for R_req; declares all three now RESOLVED/COMPLETE and issues an overall VERDICT: READY FOR RATIFICATION, citing the Structural Completeness Theorem, the complexity matrix, and the four-phase governance workflow as the satisfying evidence for each.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ratified P1 (Core Invariants) -- 7 Distinctions ... Ratified P2 (Required) -- 5 Distinctions [including D-5.2 Necessary vs. Contingent] ... Deferred to P3 (Domain-Specific) -- 2 Distinctions [D-5.1 Analytic vs. Synthetic, D-5.3 Deontic/Normative]
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the ratified distinction inventory with a tier placement that differs from the immediately preceding ratification-package file in this same batch: here D-5.2 (Necessary vs. Contingent) sits in Tier P2 (Required) rather than P3, and D-1.3 (Explicit vs. Implicit) is counted as one of 7 Tier-P1 distinctions rather than 6 -- a specific cross-document tier-placement inconsistency within this batch's ratification cluster, both nonetheless summing to '12 distinctions ratified' in each document's own status block.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 R_req -> Contr: D-1.1 (Contradictory) Detection trigger for isolation; D-3.1 (Evidential Direction) Polarity graph for resolution; D-4.1 (Resolution Status) State machine for contradiction management. 4.2 R_req -> Zero: Zero requires: D-1.1 No Contradictory or Underdetermined states; D-2.1 All propositions Current; D-1.2 All propositions have a Justification Mode; D-3.1 No Dual evidence directions. 4.3 R_req -> Evaluation: Evaluation adequacy requires: D-1.1, D-1.2, D-2.1, D-3.1, D-4.2 must be preserved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds an explicit R_req-to-subsystem integration-usage mapping not spelled out this concretely elsewhere in the batch: for Contr, D-1.1 triggers isolation detection, D-3.1 feeds the polarity graph, D-4.1 drives the contradiction-management state machine; for Zero, four specific conditions are required (no Contradictory/Underdetermined per D-1.1, all-Current per D-2.1, a Justification Mode present per D-1.2 for every proposition, no Dual evidence direction per D-3.1); for Evaluation adequacy, D-1.1/D-1.2/D-2.1/D-3.1/D-4.2 must all be preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. Compliance Criteria & Verification Standard: 1. Identity Preservation Test: Inject opposing claims p and not-p; verify S+(p) and S-(p) remain independently queryable. 2. Provenance Traceability Test: Mutate state through operation delta; verify full audit path P is reconstructible from K_{t+1}. 3. Boundary Differentiation Test: Execute depth parameter S; verify system distinguishes between direct assertion (S=0) and deep derivation (S>0). 6. Ratification Sign-off: R_req v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED as the foundational invariant for KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies three compliance verification tests for any candidate representation/kernel (Identity Preservation, Provenance Traceability, Boundary Differentiation) and issues a boxed ratification sign-off: 'R_req v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED as the foundational invariant for KnowledgeOS', naming SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 as the next required artifact -- a self-contained ratification act issued from within the same document, not an external governance-ledger entry.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There are at least four possibilities. A. Syntactic equality ... B. Semantic equality ... C. Observational equality ... D. Provenance-sensitive equality ... These are not interchangeable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four non-interchangeable candidate Knowledge-State equality relations: syntactic (byte/structural identity), semantic (same knowledge semantics), observational (same result under every permitted observation), and provenance-sensitive (content and relevant provenance equivalent).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1={p,e1} and K2={p,e2} where e1!=e2 but Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p). Should K1=K2? There is no obvious answer. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked counterexample (two states differing only in which distinct evidence item supports the same proposition) showing equality is undecidable until it is settled whether provenance is semantically constitutive of knowledge identity or merely metadata -- concluding equality is ontology/semantics-dependent, not free-standing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The mandate explicitly tells us not to assume this dependency ordering [G1->G2->G3]. ... the dependency graph is more accurately: Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality ... So G1->G3 is plausible, but G1->G2->G3 is not established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a previously assumed linear dependency ordering (G1: what is a KnowledgeState -> G2: what is epistemic status -> G3: what is equality) into a revised chain Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality, with epistemic status interacting with both representation and equality rather than sitting strictly between state-definition and equality; the direct G1->G2->G3 chain is explicitly downgraded to not established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The propositions may refer to different times ... Then there is no contradiction. This demonstrates that contradiction cannot be determined from proposition content alone. ... A better candidate is: Contradicts(p1,p2,c) ... contradiction is likely a derived semantic relation, not a primitive field o
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-interval example (HasVersion(S,v1) valid on [t1,t2), HasVersion(S,v2) valid on [t2,t3)) that two propositions with conflicting content are not automatically contradictory, since contradiction depends on context c as well as content; concludes contradiction is a derived semantic relation Contradicts(p1,p2,c), not a primitive Knowledge-State field.

b_rows_sample.anchor: with both assert validity over exactly the same interval ... If the domain invariant is: forall t: #Version(S,t)<=1, then Contradicts(p1,p2)=true. ... Contradiction required: proposition semantics; temporal validity; domain constraints. Contradiction is not merely a property of two strings.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a strong-contradiction example: two version propositions over the identical time interval, evaluated against an explicit domain invariant (a service has at most one version at any time) actually do produce Contradicts=true, demonstrating contradiction requires jointly proposition semantics, temporal validity, and domain constraints -- it is a relation evaluated under a semantic regime, not a syntactic property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A logical regime could define Contradiction_L. A temporal regime could define Contradiction_T. A probabilistic regime might instead calculate P(p1|E) and P(p2|E). These need not produce the same classification. Contradiction may be regime-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that contradiction may be regime-relative: a logical regime, a temporal regime, and a probabilistic regime applied to the same pair of propositions need not agree on whether a contradiction exists -- a stronger claim than merely 'KnowledgeOS supports contradictions', and supportive of a multi-regime architecture operating over a common substrate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(p)=0.7 ... It could represent: probability of truth; confidence in an observation; reliability of a source; posterior probability; frequency in a population; degree of belief; probability of an answer. These are mathematically different quantities. 0.7 alone has no epistemic semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues a bare numeric uncertainty value (e.g. P(p)=0.7) has no epistemic semantics on its own, since it could denote any of at least 7 mathematically distinct quantities (probability of truth, observation confidence, source reliability, posterior probability, population frequency, degree of belief, or probability of an answer) -- reinforcing an earlier corpus warning against identifying measurement/probability with knowledge itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_M(p|E) has a meaningful interpretation relative to M. This is fundamentally different from asserting p=0.7. ... K --probabilistic regime--> D ... A probability distribution may be a regime-specific representation over a knowledge-state space [not] KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution. The latter
b_rows_sample.statement: Relocates probability from being a property directly assigned to a proposition (p=0.7) to a projection K --regime--> D produced by an explicit probabilistic model M (P_M(p|E)); explicitly rejects the earlier corpus formulation 'KnowledgeOS = Application + Distribution + Measure' as a category error, preserving instead the weaker claim that a probability distribution may be one regime-specific representation over the knowledge-state space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: not every numerical assignment licenses arithmetic operations ... c(p)+c(q) is not automatically meaningful. Nor is 2c(p). Numeric representation != quantitative measurement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Invokes a Roberts-style measurement-theory constraint: a numerical assignment is meaningful only when its empirical relational structure and representation theorem justify it, so arithmetic operations on a stored confidence/uncertainty number (e.g. c(p)+c(q), 2*c(p)) are not automatically meaningful -- numeric representation is not the same as quantitative measurement, a constraint relevant to any future statistical regime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Substrate plus Semantic Relations plus Epistemic Qualifications plus Regime Specific Projections rather than one homogeneous mathematical object containing every possible quantity. ... Projection_R: K x R -> Y_R where K = knowledge substrate; R = regime; Y_R = regime-specific representatio
b_rows_sample.statement: Converges on a 4-part architectural decomposition (Knowledge Substrate, Semantic Relations, Epistemic Qualifications, Regime-Specific Projections) rather than one homogeneous state object, formalized as a candidate interface Projection_R: K x R -> Y_R (K=substrate, R=regime, Y_R=regime output), instantiated for logical (LogicalModel), probabilistic (Distribution), measurement (MeasurementSpace) and governance (Decision/ComplianceAssessment) regimes -- explicitly not yet the final architecture but a testable interface.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A regime may transform or interpret a knowledge substrate, but it must not silently change the historical identity of the underlying knowledge objects. ... the projection should preserve the identity mapping id_K: K -> K. A regime-specific representation must not silently turn e1 into e2.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a candidate cross-regime invariant: any regime projection Pi_R(K)=Y_R must preserve the identity mapping id_K:K->K on the underlying knowledge objects -- a regime interpretation must never silently substitute one evidence/knowledge object's identity for another's, which is particularly important for provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must distinguish the epistemic substrate from the mathematical regimes used to interpret it. ... Probability != Knowledge. Measurement != Knowledge. Logical inference != Knowledge. but all may operate on knowledge under properly defined regimes.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the step's central principle: KnowledgeOS must distinguish the epistemic substrate from the mathematical regimes (logical, probabilistic, measurement) used to interpret it -- Probability != Knowledge, Measurement != Knowledge, Logical inference != Knowledge, though all may legitimately operate on knowledge as regimes; noted as independently arrived at, matching an existing corpus warning against equating the epistemic core with measure theory.

b_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the next test (named Step 247, State vs. History Sufficiency Test): whether the candidate Knowledge State K_t is sufficient by itself, or whether the true formal object must be a state-history pair (K_t, H_t) with H_t=(K0,T1,...,Tt), given the corpus's repeated emphasis on provenance/transformation/history as central rather than a single lineage component.
